reading.arc: The sequence takes one verb, draw, and gives it fourteen jobs. A seed becomes a picture only through a procedure (Definition); a gauge condenses a sample and forgets its order (Entropy); a rule fixes the eligible set before chance picks, and a second piece of code turns a disappearance into a fall (Remove); two marks become contours, a floor, slabs at shoulder width and an ant's map (10 PRINT); a thrown die is read from its orientation and kept as frequencies (Cubes); turning accumulates without a trail (Rotate); a trail is kept but never consulted (Walk); a histogram's shape is a matter of law, clipping and bins (Gaussian); a wardrobe samples within a recipe that chance cannot extend (Mushrooms); neighbours share or do not (Geometry); chance gets four different jobs in a gallery (Examples); a mark enters the next decision (Pheromone); layers add up to something that looks like land (Space); and the closing crossing asks which decisions are already made and which a body must still find out (Game). The through-line is a refusal to let the word random cover three decisions at once: what may vary, how it is drawn, and what is kept. The reader is asked again and again to predict before pressing, and to compare records that forget different things.
holds: The refrain of three decisions folded into one word: "Filter, draw, delete… only the middle one is" (Remove) returns as palette / line rule / canvas (Examples), wardrobe vs construction (Mushrooms), sampling / clipping / binning (Gaussian), and stands / leaves / gone / returns (Game).

The seed as a name that is not the whole recipe: seed + generator + calls + use (Definition) → "Changing modes retains the seed but spends its draws differently" (Walk) → "a seed is not a promise that every branch of a program spends its draws in the same way" (Mushrooms), carried by a REPLAY / NEW SEED console in almost every hall (board, floor, terrarium, sampler, silhouettes, couture, crossing, doors, podium).

Records that forget different things: the gauge without order (Entropy), the glass without landing places (Cubes), the trail without its beginning (Walk), bins that move while values stay (Gaussian), scent vs raised terrain (Pheromone), counters vs the newest 300 marks (Examples).

The body as the test of a mark: slot plate vs withdrawn collider (Remove), ridges you walk through vs slabs you cannot (10 PRINT), the floor that removes support under you (Remove, returning in Game), the stone that leaves while you stand on it (Game).

Returning objects: the removal floor comes back "smaller now" in Random_Game; the entropy gauge stands again in Random_Space; the Trace drawing dot returns with a random offset; the 10 PRINT diagonals recur on the textile bolts (Definition) and the Molnar grids.
Every chapter opens by naming the previous room's move and closes by naming the next room's question, so the sequence reads as one walk rather than fourteen labels.

hall_notes.note: REPLAY, +1 DRAW and the seed slider separate a seed from the procedure that spends it; the textile bolts, the 1955 page and the crank are three ways to keep or lose a draw. The strongest opening in the sequence: predict-then-press throughout, every claim backed by the two loops it quotes.

The gauge, SORT and CONTRAST show what a categorical entropy keeps and forgets; then the jar, the displaced-point field, the ruin and the museum's own weathering wall make the omission bodily. The longest chapter: the DISCLOSE paragraph reads as a control manual, and the ruin section could lose a hundred words without losing a move.

The board makes filter, draw and delete three visible steps with a code excerpt for each, then the floor gives the same draw a consequence by withdrawing collision. Tight and exact; the ROW/COLUMN comparison under one seed is the sequence's best small experiment.

One BASIC line taken apart at its constant and its semicolon, then the same stream as Molnar grids, a floor of ridges, slabs at shoulder width and an ant's map. Reads well, but "Look down" arrives without a walk, and the slab wall it climaxes on is not yet in the museum's deal.

A thrown die read from orientation, a coin with gauges for its conditions, a heap that loses pieces and a field of bounded profiles: four records that forget different things. Short and clear; two desktop asides break the headset voice.

Rust that records your movement, then two stacks whose only change is accumulated turning under the hall's #study:rotation, then a tilt field that is a rule about place. Good comparison discipline; one sentence ("Nothing there turns") contradicts the field's clocked motion.

Steps proposed from the position reached, reflected at the glass, recorded in a trail the generator never reads; then a wandering drawing dot and a floor that rises where it is visited. Its best passage is the read-aloud of three lines; the self-avoiding sculpture, the paper rack and the leash go unplaced.

PAUSE, BATCH, the two laws' code, the u1 guard, the clip and BINS separate sampling, clipping and binning of the same stored values; the splatter's refused centre closes it. Precise and well paced; the clipped-count vs edge-bin distinction is a fine touch.

SHOW, SIZE, KIND and the named seed read a population's construction; then silhouettes (DRESS vs FORMS) and three couture bodies separate a wardrobe from a change of recipe. Long but earns it; one desktop aside.

White vs Perlin columns under SEED, FREQUENCY and OCTAVES, with the discipline of withholding the landscape reading. Reads as a bench note rather than a walk: no arrival, no placement, and in the built museum the bench stands in a wall row beside a plank over the hall's void.

Pollock homage, dartboard estimate, pipe and particle study each give chance a different job. Clear and honest about its limits (500 darts, 300 marks, 180 segments); opens with a curator's "returned".

Walkers whose deposits enter the next decision; ATTRACT vs AVOID at the same step count; the clipboard's optimal-route claim corrected in prose. A good argument whose two numbers (40 %, four walkers) do not match the field (30 %, five).
OCT, LAC and PER on a sine-based mixer, the independent-corner floor underfoot, the palette named as an interpretation. Short and sound; the Worley display and the returning gauge get no sentence.

Cycling stones with drawn waits and a tablet that shows the stored deadline, the removal floor returning, three doors decided before the press, a projectile field and a podium whose delays are drawn as a ridge. The sequence's strongest closing hall; one desktop aside, two unserved anchors, and a closer that skips the biome ladder.

stumbles: Random_Space_Geometry: the chapter opens "Look closely at neighbouring columns in the two small grids" with no arrival and no placement; in the map the bench sits at interactables (6,23) on a structure row that is wall, and the five works beyond it have no structure row at all, so the built hall puts them over a void beside a one-cell plank.

Randomness_10_PRINT_Algorithm: "Now return to the taller slabs near the entrance" sends the reader into a wall form that exists only in today's uncommitted map edit; both museum plans still deal the old hall (a science_screen and one floor-form structure).

Randomness_10_PRINT_Algorithm: "Look down. The newest seven rows of the screen are also under your feet" — the floor form stands at (11,12), eight cells from the printer at (3,11) where the reader was just told to stand.
Random_Cubes: "On a desktop the object is dropped rather than thrown" and "On a desktop, these are drops" — a headset reader is told about a rig they are not holding, twice.
Random_Pheromone: the quoted label "signal-guided: 40%" and "the four walkers" contradict the field, which prints 30 % and runs five walkers; a reader who checks the label loses trust in the rest.
Random_Rotate_Random_XYZ: "a low field of cubes begins to tilt" followed by "Nothing there turns" — the field pitches on a sine clock and the reader watching it is told nothing moves.
Randomness_Examples_of_Randomness: "Four works have returned to the gallery" — returned from where? A curation note in the reader's voice.

Random_Walk: "the grip from Trace" — the earlier room is Point_Trace, whose chapter has no title and never calls itself Trace; and the self-avoiding sculpture is introduced "between this cabinet and the basin" when it stands six cells off to the side with no anchor.
Random_Entropy: the DISCLOSE paragraph ("Press DISCLOSE… press it again… Keep pressing…") reads as a control manual inside an otherwise well-paced chapter.

Random_Game: "Press CUE again and all three stones carry a ring" implies only the middle stone had one before; the crossing builds the crown on all three stones from the start (random_cycle_cube.gd:709–714), so the reader looks for a difference that is not there.

keep.quote: Filter, draw, delete: three decisions that are easy to fold into one word, random, and only the middle one is.
Nothing in a draw says that it is red. Red is the use made of its place in these three calls.
A high reading is not a certificate of meaninglessness and a low one is not a certificate of value
Each cell was decided alone. Whether you can cross depends on their arrangement together. A body meets a consequence that no single draw contains.
No side of the cube bears that number. It belongs to a distribution, while the observed mean belongs to the throws made so far.
Read the order aloud. Keep where we were. Shorten the record. Put the bead where we are now.
A finite run need not contain such a draw; the model's tail is a probability, not an appointment.
Before describing a missed step as poor timing, ask where its warning was readable.

reading.handover_in: Clean. WaveFunctions_Synthesis_Lab ends on what must be retained to bring an unfamiliar result back, and Random_Definition opens by naming the five amounts and the familiar curve before turning to a patch of colour nobody would have chosen; the question (what does a name leave out of a making?) is exactly what the seed console answers. One blemish: the Synthesis Lab closer writes the next room as "Random_Definition", with an underscore, a file token rather than a room name, while every closer inside randomness writes room names as words ("In Random Gaussian", "in Random Space Geometry", "In Noise Types").
reading.handover_out: Random_Game closes "In Noise Types we will carry that question between neighbouring places", and Random_Noise_Types opens "The stones behind us could disappear. Their order of movement stayed intact; the drawn waits changed how long we had to cross" — an accurate recall of the crossing, and the plane-clipping point that follows is a fair next step from "which decisions are already made". But the museum deals Biome_Ladder_Randomness between the two (em_plan plans[76] → [77] nine biome vitrines → [78]), and neither chapter mentions it, whereas the Mushrooms closer names its cage interlude; the visitor walks a hall the book does not acknowledge before the promised next room.

reading.arc: The sequence begins where Randomness left off, with draws that do not consult their neighbours (a point clamped back onto a plane, a spacing rule that refuses candidates, ten thousand independent bar heights) and with sound filters that keep a previous value or subtract it, so that 'a neighbour has become a previous moment'. From the column hall on, every chapter asks the same question of a different body: what does a value become once it reaches a recipient? A phase for a column shaft, relief and colour on two rings, an added height with a collision mesh, a yes-or-no occupancy in a 24-cubed lattice, a weighted sum dressed as a wall, a borrowed address (domain warping), a ground that can refuse a foot, and finally a matched comparison of two generators. The synthesis hall ends by naming 'blob culture', the ease of the noise gesture as a habit that arrives before the next question, and a titleless corridor coda asks the reader to retell one encounter twice before cellular automata make a cell's next state depend on stored neighbours. Throughout, each control (FREEZE, RESET, MATCH, REPLAY) is introduced together with the edge of its reach, and the dark orb's own sine clock is the thing that lies outside every one of them.
holds: The dark orb in every hall, running on its own sine clock (dark_sphere.gd:599-600), used each time as the outside of a local control: FREEZE, RESET and MATCH all stop short of it, so 'a return always has a scope'.

One question carried hall to hall and stated outright in Noise_Inside_Noise's send-off: which of coordinate, value, surface and body changed, and which body makes that difference matter. Noise_Space_10 and Noise_Perlin_Simplex both open by answering it.

Carried objects across the handovers: the zero that keeps reclaiming depth, the dark patch that REMAP recovers (carried into the threshold), the rejected value (carried into abs), the occupied volume (carried back into the cave question), the small sheet's swelling surface (carried into Lab_Path and into CA_Introduction's 'keep the pleasure of the blob').

The appearance/support distinction, checked in code each time: rings and comparison spheres with no collision, a basin, a voxel volume and a walk terrain whose visible mesh is also the collider. 'What the body can cross and what it imagines crossing need not arrive together.'

The name-versus-implementation habit: 'erosion' that carries nothing anywhere, colour-noise curves that are illustrations not measurements, an artifact called perlin_noise_terrain whose helper leaves the basis at OpenSimplex2S, a display grid that is not the lattice inside the calculation.

Short verbatim code excerpts as the anchor of every claim, followed by a plain reading of the line ('Read the last line again. There is room in the vector for a third number. The code keeps writing zero there.').

hall_notes.note: Four works: the clamped point, the spaced cloud with its refused ghosts and exhausted budget, the field of ten thousand independent bars, and the five colour filters. The longest and densest hall of the sequence; the sound/image separation ('The sound is not a scan through these ten thousand heights') is its best passage, the RULE/Gaussian paragraph its hardest turn.

Three drivers (a held value, a sine, a seeded field) hand the same column recipe one number each; FREEZE, SPIN, MARBLE and REVEAL take deformation apart into transformation, material and rebuild budget. Reads clearly and warmly ('Put the veining back if you prefer it'); the synthesis-stand paragraph at the end is a detour into family/score vocabulary the reader has no handle for.

The ring pair (REMAP recovers what the clip folded together; AMPLITUDE and FREQUENCY separate the force of an appearance from the coordinate consulted; no y) and the layered basin (three authored ingredients, an 'erosion' that lowers without carrying, combine-then-modify versus modify-then-combine). The most careful hall; every number was verified against noiselayers.tscn and noisetorus.gd.

One return statement decides occupancy; bias gives the field a downstairs; pieces and occupied counts have different rhythms; CUT hides without removing; the screen sets the value beside the decision; the large volume keeps the same 13,824 answers at five times the spacing. Reads as the sequence's clearest argument, with one misplaced pointer to 'the plate' that counts.

The room wears a cloud sum: FREEZE, DRESS, LAYERS and BASIS, the abs that lets both signs dress a surface, the weights 0.5/0.75/0.9375/0.9844, the gain clamp, the separate four-term detail loop, the UV seam at each wall piece. Tight and short; one unsourced measurement clause and one 'the player' break its address.

Domain warping read as two moments, make an address then ask the base field there; ZERO/WARP/SAMPLE/RELIEF separate changing where to sample from changing what a sample does; the enclosure at 65% shares the projection. The choreography (look up, look down, follow a line) is dense but the reader is always told where to look.

The answer reaches the ground: HEIGHT, ROUTE, SAMPLE, RESET (refused while a body is on the patch), ground_at and edge_weight, the section versus a body with width, the cave a heightfield cannot hold. Strong hall weakened by a desktop walk record told in the main prose to a headset visitor.

A matched pair (same seed, octaves, frequency, gain; REPLAY, FREQ, SAMPLE, MATCH, VIEW, REGEN) and the small sheet whose timer visits another slice; closes on blob culture. The blob-culture pages are the sequence's landing; a bracketed docs URL and one sentence about REGEN trip the reader on the way there. Hands straight to Cellular Automata, skipping Lab_Path.

A coda with no title line: recall one encounter, tell it twice, 'Hold a seed. Change a threshold.', then the handover through stored state. Good pause, but the museum plan and the book both drop this hall, so the headset reader never meets it.

stumbles: Random_Noise_Types: the RULE paragraph asks the reader to hold a Gaussian draw, a clamp to the frame, shells that 'may already be red before you touch anything' and a reference distance 'the generator never promised to preserve' in one breath, just before the hands-on moment of carrying a point into a shell.

Noise_Columns: 'The stand's plaque records a chosen variant and a score from a saved comparison' arrives with variant, score and family undefined; the plaque itself prints 'dark_sphere 35%' and the reader cannot tell what the number is a percentage of.

Noise_Voxel: 'The plate counts groups joined through cell faces' sits in the large volume's section, but the volume's only plate reads 'SAME 24 x 24 x 24 CELLS | FIVE TIMES THE MODEL'; the count is on the bench readout across the room.

Noise_Space_10: 'In the recorded desktop walk, the first crossing reached the far margin' interrupts the instruction to try the crossing with somebody else's desktop session; the visitor in the headset has just been asked to walk it themselves.

Noise_Perlin_Simplex: 'The seed stays where you left it, even after REGEN' reads as a contradiction, because REGEN is the button that draws a fresh seed; the sentence is about VIEW not restoring anything, but says so only by implication.

Noise_Perlin_Simplex: the sentence-fragment '[The engine's noise definitions](https://docs.godotengine.org/...)' is a bracketed URL in wall text; a headset visitor cannot follow it and it reads as a citation pasted into prose.

Noise_Perlin_Simplex to Lab_Path: 'In the next chapter, Cellular Automata' is followed, in the sequence's map order, by a chapter that is not Cellular Automata; the reader then gets a second send-off to the same place.
Lab_Path: the chapter opens without a heading, mid-thought ('What has followed you out of the room?'), unlike every other chapter in the sequence.

Noise_6_Wall: 'even their brightest pixel reached only about half-white' is the one measurement in the sequence with no date or method, in a hall that footnotes nothing while its neighbours footnote every number.

keep.quote: What looks like a flat existence takes repeated work to maintain. The engine has not forgotten a dimension. This small procedure keeps declining it.
Our time for searching has ended before our question about space has been settled.
We are not obliged to hear these as damaged signals. A hiss can be a material to approach, sustain, combine, or leave. The question of what a body may do includes what it may want to remain with.
The fixed reference is itself a made body. We have chosen something to keep still so that another change can become legible.
A different reading has made room for something that was already being computed.
There is pleasure in a cavity before its usefulness is settled.
Grey is already an interpretation, with its own capacity to lose a difference. There is no final undressed picture waiting underneath every other picture.

After several rooms, that usefulness can become a mental algorithmic wall. The familiar answer arrives before we have worked out the next question. Different bodies acquire a family resemblance. We can call this tendency blob culture and begin investigating it here, among our own objects.

reading.handover_in: Clean. Random_Game closes with 'Which decisions are already made, which are still to come, and what tells us the difference? In Noise Types we will carry that question between neighbouring places', and Random_Noise_Types opens by recalling the stones ('Their order of movement stayed intact; the drawn waits changed how long we had to cross') before narrowing to 'what can change at all'. The one soft spot: the promised 'neighbouring places' only arrive at the second bench (the spacing rule); the first work is about a discarded dimension, so a reader looking for the promised neighbour waits about five hundred words.
reading.handover_out: Strong in substance, doubled in form. Noise_Perlin_Simplex ends on blob culture and 'In the next chapter, Cellular Automata, a row waits for its first update... Bring the pleasure of the moving surface, and leave room for another form'; Lab_Path ends 'Bring one of your unfinished questions with you'; CA_Introduction opens 'We have carried noise a long way: across a sheet, into a volume, around the body and under a foot... Keep the pleasure of the blob. Bring an unfinished question with it', answering both. But Lab_Path is listed in noise.json's maps while ada_run/em_plan.json deals Noise_Perlin_Simplex straight into CA_Introduction and commons/data/book/noise.json marks the Lab_Path pearl drop:true, so the headset reader gets one coherent handover and never sees the coda, while a reader following the sequence file gets two send-offs and an untitled chapter between them.

reading.arc: The sequence takes the reader out of Lab_Path's pause and through eight halls that each add one distinction to a question CA_Introduction names at its close: what a cell can hold, which neighbours it consults, and when its answer becomes available to others. A 32-cell ring rewritten row by row and a mirrored rug open it; a 3D volume adds a fading state that is present but no longer counted; a Rule 30 history is laid out as desk, stepping tiles and lattice so that depth does the work of time; a Life dish wires three fixed addresses to lamps so a travelling pattern can be told apart from the cells it visits; a graded bridge takes the visitor's own body as input and exposes the update schedule (SYNC versus SCAN); a two-concentration field shows that exchange, not a threshold, carries the difference; Rule 90 is set beside a recursive pyramid to test resemblance against procedure; and a matched pair of volumes follows one changed value under integer versus fractional storage. Every hall refuses the 'it is alive' reading and replaces it with an inspectable relation, and every local study holds at a budget while the museum's clock continues. It hands Fractals the distinction between resembling a neighbour, inheriting a state, and being told to repeat.
holds: The three carried choices (what a cell can hold / which neighbours / when the answer becomes available), stated at the end of CA_Introduction; each later hall alters exactly one of them.

The two-buffer refrain: 'All the questions go to the old row' (Introduction) → 'the arrays exchange places' (ElementaryRules) → the dish's two buffers (BeyondBinary) → SYNC/SCAN and 'previous if snapshot_reads else next' (ExpandingSpace) → 'separate next arrays' (SoftRules) → 'Every cell reads the previous volume' (EdgeOfChaos).

Local clock versus museum clock: every study HOLDS at a budget (24 rows, 20 steps, 48 generations, 30 simulated seconds, 2,400 updates, 100 updates) 'while the museum continues'; the phrase recurs almost verbatim in six halls.

One followed witness per hall: the pink/gold marks on the explorer, the gold line on the bridge, squares A/B/C on the Life floor, W on the decaying bridge, W on the two field tables, the lit difference in the paired volumes.

The refusal of the living reading, restated once per hall in the same key ('We need not turn that pleasure into proof of a living creature'; 'without deciding that a responsive surface must be alive').
The dark orb carried in from Lab_Path: placed in halls 1-5 (dark_sphere in CA_Introduction, CA_ElementaryRules, CA_GameOfLife, CA_BeyondBinary, CA_ExpandingSpace) but named only in the first two.

hall_notes.note: Three works (rule explorer, Persian rug, line network) plus a closing tour of the rest; nearly twice the length of any other hall. It carries the sequence's strongest sentences and its first full lesson (the two-row update, the index byte, the mirror, growth versus drawing), but the first button is pressed only after a noise recap and a riddle about which work 'has left you time to answer'.

One work, one thread: the fading state that is present but not counted, the shell renderer that hides enclosed cells, the no-wrap edge. Reads cleanly; the VIEW and CHANGED passages turn readouts into questions rather than instructions.

The Rule 30 history worn three ways (desk bars, support tiles over a basin, lattice). The opening two sentences are the best entry in the sequence. It re-teaches the index weighting from hall 1, and stops at the bridge although the hall runs on for sixteen more cells of unnamed works, including a lab whose signage claims Turing completeness.

Life in a dish, a floor-sized present, three opal lamps on fixed addresses. The address/pattern distinction lands, and LINK/MEET is the sequence's best small experiment (one-way traffic between simulation and room). One number is loose: the MEET field empties at generation six, not 'by 24'.

The visitor's body becomes an input. The three-threshold passage (0.5 to help, 0.3 to carry, 0.2 to collide) and the CHAIN/SYNC/SCAN/REVERSE comparison are exact against the code and read as the sequence's pivot from watching to being counted.

Two 32x32 fields, one with exchange and one without, mounted on tables and again on curved walls; the exchange lesson and the reviser's added sentence (the seeded square fades without exchange) both hold. The clockmaker coda is short and honest about a still diagram. Two bare names (Gray–Scott, Lenia) and one misdirection about where W is.

The explorer again, set beside the Sierpinski pyramid; a brief comparison chapter that names where the analogy stops (the cubes do not shrink with the spacing). The footnote refutes claims the chapter never made, though the explorer's own plate prints 'Turing Complete' when 110 is pressed.

A matched pair of 11-cubed volumes, one address changed, integer versus fractional storage. The fork line and the 27-address/0.75 arithmetic are the clearest code-to-consequence passage in the sequence. The closing names a hall name the visitor is never shown and the next hall by its map identifier.

stumbles: CA_Introduction: 1,262 words against 537-874 elsewhere; the reader arrives holding Lab_Path's 'unfinished question' and waits through a noise recap and 'Begin with the one that has left you time to answer' before touching the board.

CA_Introduction and CA_AgentsCircuits: 'Begin with Rule 90', 'Choose Rule 30', 'Set the rule explorer to Rule 90' — the rules are numeral buttons (30, 90, 110, 184, RST) on a second panel with two sliders, while STEP/RUN/SEED/CELL live on the study panel; the prose never says there are two panels.

CA_GameOfLife: after the bridge the visitor crosses sixteen unnarrated cells holding the columns, the orb, an 8 x 7 m 'TURING MACHINE LAB' whose signage reads 'Rule 110 → universal computation' and 'Game of Life is Turing complete', and a mirrored automaton — the loudest text in the hall asserts what the sequence's own footnote declines.

CA_BeyondBinary: 'by generation 24 the field is empty' — it is empty from generation six; and lamp A is lit before the first step because the block sits on A, which the prose leaves for the reader to discover as a surprise rather than a prediction.
CA_SoftRules: 'At the side desk, find W' sends the reader to the console for a gold cross that is on the two tables; only its readings are on the desk.
CA_SoftRules: 'Lenia' arrives as a bare name; 'Gray–Scott' is named without attribution or the source of feed .037 / kill .060.

CA_AgentsCircuits: the footnote argues against 'an agent, a circuit or a general-purpose computer' — nobody in the chapter said so; the words the visitor actually meets are the plate's 'RULE 110 / Turing Complete' and 'RULE 90 / Sierpiński'.

CA_EdgeOfChaos: 'The hall is called Edge of Chaos' — the museum prints no hall names (the threshold plaque was retired as 'no labels in space'), and the chapter's own title is 'How far does one difference go?'; then 'The next hall, Fractal_Recursion' is a file identifier in reader prose.
Sequence-wide: 'Rule 30/90/110' is used throughout with no mention of Wolfram or of how the 256 are numbered beyond the byte in the excerpt.
CA_GameOfLife: the 4/2/1 index weighting and the `100` versus `001` comparison repeat what CA_Introduction taught two halls earlier with `100` versus `010`.

keep.quote: A neighbourhood is already a decision about what information may matter.
Once again, the visible past is smaller than the past that brought us here.
Being present and being counted have parted company.
A gap in the screen lets you see through. The same gap in the floor asks something else of your body.
A zero does not contain an instruction to make a hole.
The rule includes a schedule, even when the picture conceals it.
More places carry it. Less of it remains at any one place.
We have measured some consequences of those choices. We have not located the one permissible region where life, computation or queerness can exist.

reading.handover_in: Clean. Lab_Path closes with 'That previous step has to be kept while the next one is written' and 'Bring one of your unfinished questions with you'; CA_Introduction answers both literally ('Bring an unfinished question with it'; 'All the questions go to the old row'), and its noise recap ('across a sheet, into a volume, around the body and under a foot') is the noise halls in walking order. The dark orb that Lab_Path centres on reappears on the rug's edge. The only cost is that the recap delays the first instruction (see the CA_Introduction structure task).
reading.handover_out: The distinction CA_EdgeOfChaos hands over — 'a form can resemble its neighbour, inherit an earlier state, or be told to repeat' — is exactly what Fractal_Recursion opens on ('Here is the self-call'; 'Seeing a square inside another square does not tell us which program made it'), so the join works. Two soft spots: the closing names the next hall by its map identifier (Fractal_Recursion), and Fractal_Recursion's 'We already met this gap at the trace' leans on CA_EdgeOfChaos's single use of 'trace' (a difference leaving the counter before the stored values), which a reader may not connect. CA_AgentsCircuits' promise to 'return to the pyramid's way of making in Fractals' is kept by a later fractal hall (the pyramid's identity names Fractal_KochSierpinski), not by the first, which is acceptable since it names the sequence.
reading_errors: CA_ExpandingSpace hall note: 'The three-threshold passage (0.5 to help, 0.3 to carry, 0.2 to collide) … exact against the code' — the code has TWO thresholds: a neighbour counts toward recovery only above 0.5 (decaying_bridge.gd:100) and below 0.2 the collider is disabled and the tile goes translucent (decaying_bridge.gd:130-135); carrying and colliding are the same 0.2 threshold (proximity_study.gd:93, supported = h >= 0.2). 0.3 is an illustrative value in the chapter, which itself says 'One changing value meets two different thresholds' (final.md:28).

Holds, local clock: 'every study HOLDS at a budget (24 rows, 20 steps, 48 generations, 30 simulated seconds, 2,400 updates, 100 updates)' — the 100 is difference_model.gd:7 (LIMIT = 100) and is never stated in the CA_EdgeOfChaos chapter, which says only 'a larger one whose clock continues'; five of the six numbers are in the chapters, not six.

Holds, refusal of the living reading 'restated once per hall in the same key' — CA_AgentsCircuits has no living-reading sentence; its refusal (final.md:27) is of agent/circuit/computer claims, and CA_Introduction's nearest line is 'Their resemblance to living things can invite us closer' (:75). Six halls, not eight.

Arc: 'takes the reader out of Lab_Path's pause' holds in book/sequence order (Lab_Path is the last map of the noise sequence, noise.json maps[49]) but not in the museum: Lab_Path is not a dealt hall — em_plan.json names it only as an inactive teleporter ('Lab Path - not connected') in Noise_Perlin_Simplex's row — so the museum walker enters CA_Introduction from Noise_Perlin_Simplex.

Minor: the hall-note word counts differ from a recount (code, anchors and comments excluded) by up to five words (Introduction 1,260 not 1,262; ElementaryRules 745 not 750; SoftRules 871 not 874) — tokenisation noise, not an error, but the figures should not be quoted as exact.

reading.arc: The sequence takes one instruction, call yourself again, and walks it through seven halls, asking at every desk what the call costs and what it leaves a body. It opens with a single self-call (nested squares), four self-calls (rings), a subdivision spent one cell at a time (DRILL and SPREAD buy different bodies for the same 85 cells) and a chair that is recursive in name only; then the call acquires a start, a direction and a length (trees); then a generation that removes (the Cantor bar, and a pagoda whose gaps admit some bodies and refuse others); then a boundary that lengthens (Koch) beside a surface that empties (Sierpinski), a measuring bench whose slope moves with the fit, and a pyramid built with one call more than its recipe promised. Removal then enters a volume the visitor can fly through (Menger), repetition becomes number and the mapping that gives number a height (Fibonacci towers, the golden rectangle), and a synthesis hall asks the visitor to say a rule without its name before handing one explicit rule to the grammar laboratory. The through-argument is that the count, the drawn record and what a body can use are three resolutions that never coincide, and that a resemblance (tree, shell, chair, pyramid) tells you nothing about the procedure until you look behind the image.
holds: One desk grammar: a compact six-key console at every work (NEXT/BACK, two instrument keys, RESET, RULE) with a readout that counts and a RULE key that shows the source line; the visitor learns the desk in the first hall and meets it in all seven (recursion_lesson, recursive_tree_lesson, cantor_lesson, koch_sierpinski_lesson, menger_lesson, golden_mapping_lesson all build the same console).
Predict before you press: every desk asks for a number before the button (five rings, twenty-one, thirty-one segments, 2^n pieces, 216 to 125) and then shows where the count and the body diverge.

Three resolutions, carried from the trace hall: what is stored, what is drawn, and what becomes available to a body; re-measured at each work (341 rings the room can hold, 63 bars once history is drawn, 216 overlapping cubes, a one-metre opening light passes and a body does not).

The removed part made visible: GHOST/SCAR/GONE on the chair, GHOST on the bar and the sponge, VIEW on the triangle; absence drawn without collision, and then a passage (the pagoda gap, the sponge cross) where an absence becomes a place.

Resemblance is not procedure: a chair with no self-call, a block tree that persuades us it is organic, a shell and a seed head, a helix that is not a golden spiral, a pyramid whose name outran its recipe; each hall keeps the recognition and asks what supplied it.

The finite instrument against the limit: each desk names its cap (seven levels, five cuts, four replacements, two cuts) and says in one sentence that the limit is not what the headset contains or the body touches.

hall_notes.note: Four desks, one question: what a self-call costs. Squares (one call, LAYOUT and COLLAPSE), rings (four calls, PACKING and TURN), a cube split one selected cell at a time (DRILL versus SPREAD end on the same 85 cells with different bodies) and a chair whose five authored stages contain no self-call. Dense but paced by prediction prompts; the strongest opening for the stored/drawn/body distinction, and all numbers check against the code.

The call gets a start, a direction and a length. A deterministic growing tree (GROW, ANGLE through 15/35/65, LENGTH 0.70/0.85/0.50, FORKS 2 or 3: 31 to 121 segments) beside a seeded block tree read through STRATA, REACH and ENDS. Tight and clear; the closing question about a fork becoming shelter carries the body thread forward.

Removal as generation. The bar desk (six metres, five cuts, 32 pieces under a metre, 63 bars once history is counted), then the pagoda whose openings of 3 m, 1 m and a third of a metre admit different bodies. The best-embodied hall: the proxy-body paragraph is the sequence's thesis in one place, and the ramp up to the deck is real (two walkway cells).

Four instruments: Koch's detour (256 segments, 12.6 m of path between ends 4 m apart), Sierpinski's removals that VIEW can turn into the work, a box-counting bench whose reported slope moves with RANGE, and a pyramid with one call too many (216 to 125 instances). The longest hall by a third; it reads as two halls, and the pyramid's withheld comparison, the peak of the sequence, arrives when attention is lowest.

One work, two cuts, and a body that flies. 729 to 540 to 400 cubic metres, seven then 140 ghosts, a twelve-metre glass enclosure whose two ground doors bound the flight, a desk that refuses to rebuild while someone is inside. Reads well until the locomotion paragraph, which becomes a manual for a desktop body the headset reader does not have.

Number and mapping. Towers whose heights HEIGHT re-maps (half a metre for a one under the log rule, five centimetres per unit under the linear one), SUM stacks that check the recurrence in units, then a five-metre rectangle cut by squares of 3.090, 1.910 and 1.180 m with quarter-circle ARCs. Careful about resemblance (shell, seed head, helix versus spiral); long because it carries two works and the held examples, and one of its comparisons has no body in the room.

Say the rule without its name. The bar and the block tree return on the same desks; the chapter asks what a description omits (how short, at which ends, what a call must remember to place a branch) and hands one explicit rule, F to F+F-F-F+F at ninety degrees, to the grammar laboratory. Quiet, reflective, the right length.

keep.quote: Seeing a square inside another square does not tell us which program made it. We had to look behind the image.
Equal counts have bought different bodies.
The display can remember an absence without filling it with something that supports a body.
All are gaps. They do not all admit the same body.
The unoccupied cells tell us where this reading found no points. They have no authority over what may exist.
There was a connection in the geometry. There was not yet a route for every body.
We can change the representation without changing the relation it represents. We can also lose sight of a small value without removing it from the sequence.
The queer possibility here is a question we can keep material: which instruction would have to change for another body to have room?

reading.arc: The sequence takes one object out of the fractal halls, a sentence read by a turtle, and splits it into the two moments that were fused there: rewriting the sentence and reading it as movement. Each hall then adds one thing the bare grammar leaves out. Grammar Lab separates NEXT from TURN with HOLD as a witness; Growth follows the saved state through a bracket and lets length inherit; Grammars_And_Curves shows that even 'forward' is an assignment the reader makes; Architecture gives the line width, walls, rooms and a body that must fit; Competition gives the same rule a shared field and a turn order; Living goes behind the grammar to the raw gene and the counting threshold; Shape Grammars moves the rule from letters to faces and enlarges the result until the visitor stands beneath it; Assemblage closes on two marks and the paths a viewer reads into them. The question the sequence keeps asking, in nearly every closing paragraph, is what would have to be added before any of these drawings could hold, shelter, admit or obstruct a body. It is disciplined, checkable and unusually consistent in voice; its weaknesses are local (one desktop sentence, one unnamed button, two dangling callbacks, two missing attributions) rather than structural.
holds: The refrain 'these thin drawings have no collision surfaces / not yet somewhere to stand' closes Grammar Lab, Growth and Grammars_And_Curves, becomes the whole experiment in Architecture (a width and a body), returns as 'the floor stays solid' in Assemblage, and is picked up by Genetic Evolution's opening.
HOLD as a carried device: a witness copy of the current reading in Grammar Lab, Growth, Living and Assemblage; Living names it 'a witness', Assemblage cites Living for it, Genetic Evolution keeps it.

The bracket stack as the carried object: saved and restored state named at the end of Grammar Lab ('Carry the bracket into the next room'), enacted in Growth, re-read in Curves, given an address in Architecture, called 'the familiar brackets' in Competition, and found again inside Living's instrument.

The experimental form 'same X, different Y' at every desk: same sentence / different angle; same sentence / different reader; same grammar / different soil and turn order; same gene / different rounding; same samples / different marks.

Metres against fitting: Grammar Lab declares both drawings 'fitted to their display'; Growth and Curves put metre rulers beside unfitted readings; the distinction between what is drawn and what is measured runs to the 4x canopy in Shape Grammars and the 4x branch displays in Competition.
Every chapter ends by naming the next hall and the question it will carry, so the walk reads as one argument rather than eight exhibits.

hall_notes.note: Opens the sequence at one desk with two plinths and separates rewriting (NEXT) from interpretation (TURN), with HOLD as the witness; every count in it (five segments, 49 symbols / 25 instructions, four generations, 4,096 budget, 120 visible symbols) is checkable against grammar_lesson.gd and lsystem_editor.gd. Tight and well paced; it ends by handing the bracket to Growth.

Steps through F[+F]F[-F]F one symbol at a time in metres, making the stack and the inherited length (0.800 to 0.576) concrete, then turns length_decay above 1.0 into a small surprise (0.92 m branches, a 7.2 m trunk). The most instrument-like chapter and the one whose numbers are most carefully earned; its only slips are cosmetic.

Three readers of one sentence: reference, changed angle, and the x/y exchange. Its best move is reading the 'believing' turtle as a reflection across x = y that keeps lengths, angles and connectivity. Slightly abstract in the middle, and the reader is asked to verify a geometric claim by matching forks in the headset with no figure to check against.

The plan acquires width, walls, rooms and a boundary policy; the two-R / one-address trick and the 'leave the frame before you rebuild' rule are strong and both are real in the code. Contains the sequence's one desktop sentence, which is also wrong for the headset body, and the closing list of the rear collection omits a hatch and a vent that a visitor will meet.

A controlled pair on shared soil, with order, season and soil separated into buttons; the 2.250 / 1.980 uptakes reproduce exactly from the 5x5 sampling square and the one-cell offset in ForestCompetition.gd. Reads cleanly except that the button that takes a turn (STEP) is never named.

Goes behind the grammar to the raw gene and its rounding threshold (4.8 rounds to 2, 5.0 to 3), then HOLD and PLANT as witnesses that had to be written as copies. Conceptually the richest hall; weakened by one callback with no antecedent and a 'push to the upper limits' instruction that the compact desk makes laborious.

Two works and four served figures: the family of six cubes is patient and exact (0.4 m extrusion, 8% and 28% inset, twelve faces), and the canopy's 'Walk beneath it' is the sequence's one bodily reversal. Half again as long as any other chapter, and the closing paragraph spends itself on cross-references to Form Finding and Genetic Evolution rather than on the hall.

Closes on two marks and reader-made paths: ALPHABET holds the choices, ODDS holds the samples, STEP discards a row, and the floor pattern makes 'no collision boundary follows these lines' walkable. The coda on the loom and the galleries is generous and correctly attributed to Kristina Torsson, but the textile's own source, 10 PRINT, is never named although the exhibit label says it.

keep.quote: Our eyes receive a composed result: rewriting, interpretation, fitting, thickness, light. None is the untouched original behind the others.
F still means draw forward, but how far forward now depends on the state in which the turtle reads it.
The commitment is executable: F is assigned a direction through this code. We can change that assignment. We can also ask what the change has left untouched.
A plan can be legible to an eye long before it is usable by a body.
A body can remain visibly still while changing the conditions around it. To discover that here, we needed the field as well as the tree.
A control's appearance cannot tell us what kind of change it offers.
The form stays still; your movement changes what covers you.
The pleasure of finding a way through need not disappear when we learn how little the generator knew about it.

Grammar Lab opens on exactly that preset at generation zero (grammar_lesson.gd:34-36 sets preset 0, generations 0; lsystem_editor.gd:103 confirms the name, rule and 90 degrees), says 'We brought a construction out of the fractal halls', and asks 'Can one sentence have two bodies?'. reading.arc: The sequence moves from selection to inhabitation. It opens by letting a score choose among described bodies and asking what that score cannot notice (a drawn torus the estimator never counts), then makes growth explicit as target assignment and summed unit directions (Space Colonization), narrows it to one nearest invitation and discovers that stored records and visible positions can diverge (Branching Growth), tests connection under a stated rule of contact (Percolation), asks a rule to carve room for a body (Caves / Mazes), samples and cuts material (Sculpted Forms), and closes by composing copying with connecting (Mirrored Patterns). The refrain throughout is that a record, a picture and a place to stand are three different relations that must each be built and checked; the museum's own floor, ramps and decks supply the support the generated things never do. Every hall is a six-button desk with a RULE card that reveals the operation only after the visitor has followed it, and every chapter asks for a prediction or a choice before the first press.
holds: The HOLD witness on a side plinth, inherited from LSystems_Living through Assemblage: Genetic, Space Colonization, Branching and Mirrored each keep an independent copy that survives RESET ('the held witness remains').

Predict before you press: choose a body and remember your reason; which way would you go; find the nearest point; where could something pass; look for the space that would have to remain empty; choose the moment the next construction inherits.
The six-button desk with RULE last: the operation is named only after it has been followed, and each chapter quotes one or two lines of the running source at the moment they matter.

Support versus generation: decks and ramps carry the visitor because the museum supplies collision; candidates, drawn branches, pink flowing sites, the sampled surface and the observation specimen do not. 'A connected parent record, a visible shape and a place you can inhabit are three relations we must learn to build together.'
Budgets are not maturity: 192 nodes / 60 generations, 192 records, 64 generations, 128 maze steps are named as what the program spends.
Each chapter ends by naming the next hall and the smaller difference to look for there, until the last one, which summarises the sequence without naming Soft Bodies.

hall_notes.note: Opens the sequence by asking the visitor to choose a body before the score does, then uses TARGET, RING, RULE and STEP to expose the seam between builder and evaluator: a torus is drawn but never counted, a box's volume is scale product times eight, overlaps are never subtracted. The best-argued chapter; its second paragraph is the one place it looks backward too far, and the raised deck it sends you to carries a screen it never mentions.

The construction chapter: three requests, unit vectors, a sum, one 0.5 m step, predicted before it is pressed, then FIELD (8 points, a 96-point sine-authored canopy) and POLICY (tips versus network). Reads as a careful demonstration whose numbers all hold; the first instruction names colours the hall does not draw that way.

Short and sharp: one nearest invitation, a predicted (-0.4, 0.3, 0), and the discovery that the readout's records and its distinct positions need not agree because an old site keeps re-choosing the same target. The sequence's best 'useful failure'; one code token leaks into the prose.

Face versus corner contact, the six-neighbour excerpt, LATTICE and DENSITY at 0.2 / 0.4 / 0.6 from one seed, and the collision distinction (white collides, pink does not). Tight and true; 'z face' is a code axis the visitor cannot see.

Two generators in one hall: carving centres with two cells of headroom versus backtracking that pops a stack. The stack excerpt lands well and the cave's authored bias is honestly named; the closing paragraph lets the author's desktop test harness into the reader's ear.

DROP, SAMPLE, VOXEL and ORIGINAL make 'what did the sample keep' concrete (centres, not rotations or contact shapes), and the dome's CUT shows absence as authored. Weak spots: the subtraction excerpt is the section view's cutter, not a core's, and 'repaired scene' is a process note.

Holding a field and stencilling it isolates copying from updating; NETWORK counts edges, components and cycles and refuses to let a skin certify a route. Ends with the sequence's summary sentence but names neither the desk's own word 'rhizome' nor the hall the thread goes to next.

stumbles: PG_Genetic_Evolution: the second paragraph stacks five back-references (rewriting a description, the cube family, altered amount / face selection, six kept results, the Form Finding height test) before the room's own idea; the visitor arriving from the textile hall must recall two halls back and eight sequences back.
PG_Genetic_Evolution: 'take the side ramp onto the raised structure' leads straight to a cased science screen (map row 22) that the chapter never places; a reader may take it for part of the lesson.
PG_Space_Colonization: 'The gold lines show those requests' — the threads to the points are drawn in muted mauve; the gold marks are the short unit-direction stubs and the chosen site.
PG_Space_Colonization: 'a restriction easy to miss in the name of this artifact' — the chapter never says the name.
PG_Branching_Growth: 'Keep the nearby organic_space in view' reads as a variable name.
PG_Percolation_Network: 'supplied from one z face' and 'the opposite face' — the visitor sees a 9 m cube with a source wall, not an axis.
PG_Caves_Mazes: 'The desktop check follows open maze cells from entrance to exit' — a headset visitor has no desktop check; this is the author's test record.
PG_Sculpted_Forms: the excerpt cut.operation = CSGShape3D.OPERATION_SUBTRACTION is introduced as the cores' operation but is the section view's extra cutter.
PG_Sculpted_Forms: 'Its repaired scene' — the reader never saw it broken.

PG_Mirrored_Patterns: the desk readout prints 'rhizome' while the chapter says 'the next policy'; and the closing paragraph carries 'the unresolved part into the next hall' without naming Soft Bodies, the only chapter in the sequence not to name its successor.

keep.quote: This is what fitness means in this room. We can inspect it without agreeing that it measures what we value.
Survival does not tell us that every surviving feature was rewarded.
A distant point will not get a longer vote merely because it is farther away.
A connected parent record, a visible shape and a place you can inhabit are three relations we must learn to build together.
The remainder is not always an extravagant shape. Sometimes it is redundant work concealed by a familiar outline.
The same event is connection for one system and a change of resistance for another.
A connected line has no width. Your shoulders do.
A hole can carry as much authorship as the material around it.

What changes when a program is asked to decide which result should continue?' and PG_Genetic_Evolution opens by asking the visitor to choose a body and remember the reason before the score picks. The only friction is that Genetic's second paragraph reaches past Assemblage to the cube family (LSystems_Shape_Grammars, two halls back) and the Forge's height test (FormFinding_Forge, eight sequences back) without naming either hall; Shape Grammars line 61 had already made that bridge.

PG_Mirrored_Patterns closes with the sequence summary and 'carry the unresolved part into the next hall' but does not name Soft Bodies; SoftBodies_Soft_Body_Deformation opens on the jelly cube and reaches back to 'translation, rotation and scale' (line 17) rather than to anything in this sequence. The shared thread is present on both sides — positions moving while connectivity stays prescribed; collider, support and pinned points as the body's conditions — but neither chapter states it, so the reader crosses the seam unaccompanied for the first time in seven halls.

reading.arc: The sequence takes a body from a single yielding cube to a surface cut out of a field. It opens by asking what holds a deformable thing together (three coefficients on a desk, a mill that can be halted while the sphere goes on moving), then which points are forbidden to move (pins against a support that turns out to be scenery), then what changes when the support itself is driven (the carousel), when the architecture is the body (breathing walls), how to compare contacts honestly (a gallery with replay, hold and variation), and what a frozen form keeps of the process that made it (an instrument that feeds back on its own reading, a vessel reconstructed at 40/200/400 steps). It then turns on resemblance itself: radiolaria that look alive without any simulation. Two field-to-form mappings close it, Gray-Scott chemistry and a gyroid whose master control is called entropy, and the last hall asks who connected the controls. The discipline throughout is that every control is described by what it does and what it does not do, so the reader learns to separate material, boundary, drive, contact, instrument and name.
holds: The desk: every hall carries the same soft_workshop_console with five or six named controls, a two-line readout and a RULE card; the prose addresses the controls in capitals, so the reader always knows what is at hand.

The refrain 'it does X; it does not do Y' (RESET restores coefficients, not vertices; STOP zeroes the rate, not velocity or gravity; HOLD DRIVE holds phase, not vertices; RELEASE restores pins, not an original body; FEEDBACK off restores pressure, not the body you had).

Carried objects: the four stopped spheres (softstopscene) stand in Cloth and return in Reaction as 'soft-body samples'; radiolaria is flagged in hall 1 as a warning to keep for later and delivered in hall 7; the entropy surface stands in Playground as 'field sculpture' before its own hall; the cloth strips carry from Cloth into Carousel.

The pin thread: pinned points named as part of the cube's conditions, then PINS eight-two-none, then a driven pin, then pinned wall edges, then HOLD pinning every vertex, then the vessel's pinned upper region.
The resemblance-versus-mechanism thread: 'Calling it breathing is an invitation to bodily recognition', radiolaria's 'recognition before explanation', the parameter 'called entropy in the source'.
Each chapter ends by naming the next hall's question, and each title is a question the hall answers with a control.

hall_notes.note: Opens with the cube yielding and the three coefficients (stiffness, damping, pressure; all three assignments verified in jelly_cube.gd:79/87/95), then the mill whose drive can be held while the sphere's physics continues. Reads cleanly and plants radiolaria as a warning for later; it reaches back to Transformation rather than receiving the previous sequence's closing question.

The strongest chapter and more than twice the length of the others: eight strips, a support that vanishes while the held edge stays, the pin rule shown in code (exactly soft_workshop.gd:95-97; 8 of 112 vertices per strip, PlaneMesh 6x12 subdivisions), PINS eight-to-two, RELEASE, REBUILD, then the four stopped spheres. One instruction order is wrong (LANDING removes the rail before the reader is told to watch the rail) and the last line promises the wrong hanging body for the next hall.

Driven hub in radians per second (revolving_joy_ride.gd:15, 293), SPEED/REVERSE/STOP each described by what they leave running; a short, clear chapter that correctly says the cloth beside it keeps a fixed support and lists the sticks, cubes, flex pad and mushroom that are actually on the map.

The sine-to-pressure bridge is exact (breathing_room_scene.gd:12-13) and the 'invitation to bodily recognition' paragraph is the sequence's ethical centre. It names three of the desk's five controls and closes with the builder phrase 'the museum crossing', which a visitor cannot parse.

Replay, variation, hold, release and group are all real and all rebuild (softbody_test_gallery.gd:665-689); the named cells belong to the visible group. Reads as a careful method chapter about not mistaking proximity for a controlled comparison; only the example name 'Jelly' is from a group the reader is not looking at.

The instrument that measures an axis-aligned box (rounded_softbody.gd:757-767) and then feeds back on it is the sequence's sharpest idea, and the vessel section is right about closed topology and collision. It tells the reader SQUEEZE changes a strength without ever saying how a hand squeezes.

Recognition before explanation; the claim that COLOUR rebuilds geometry under an unpinned seed is true (radiolaria.gd:1157-1167 regenerates; seed 0 leaves the RNG unseeded). Short, exact, and it names its own place in the arc as a contrast, not a soft body.

Gray-Scott update, double buffering, wrapped edges and clamping all match turing_pattern_generator.gd:439-461. It alludes to the 100 STEPS button without naming it and invokes Turing and Gray-Scott with no attribution in a corpus that footnotes such names.

The lerp lines are exact (entropy_morphogenesis_vr.gd:172-174) and the closing paragraph is the sequence's summary. The LEVEL control it advertises silently fails on its fourth press, and 'the player' is the one lapse from the sequence's 'your body' vocabulary.

stumbles: SoftBodies_Cloth_Physics: 'Watch one meet the rail' follows the instruction to press LANDING, and the first press replaces the rail with the pan.

SoftBodies_Cloth_Physics to SoftBodies_Carusell: 'this time the cloth will know', but the driven support in the next hall carries soft spheres; the cloth there keeps a fixed support, as the next chapter itself says.
SoftBodies_Obsticals: 'the museum crossing still has independent support' is builder vocabulary from the map's design notes, never defined for a visitor.

keep.quote: Boundary conditions are not a detail of the setup. Here they are most of what you have been looking at.
A convincing support does not prove how a simulation is attached to it. You have just taken the support away and watched the attachment survive it.
Two questions leave this room together. What makes a body deform, and what makes us stop looking?
A soft appearance does not announce every freedom a body possesses.
A number that helped us look has become a number the body is asked to follow.
A frozen result lets us look longer. It also makes the timing of a decision disappear into the apparent permanence of a thing.
Desire can travel ahead of an explanation; a strange body can invite attention before we know how to describe it.
The point is not to exhaust desire by naming every rule. It is to gain enough purchase on a rule to change what it permits—and notice what the next construction still leaves out.

reading.handover_in: PG_Mirrored_Patterns closes: 'we have selected, guided, branched, connected, carved, sampled and copied... What bodies are possible now? We can answer with a construction, try its limits, and carry the unresolved part into the next hall.' SoftBodies_Soft_Body_Deformation opens with a cube that gives way, which does answer the question, but it never receives it: its only backward reference is 'We have already changed whole objects by translation, rotation and scale', two sequences back. The bodies thread is implicit; one sentence would make it explicit.
reading.handover_out: Strong and verified. Topology_Entropy_Morphogenesis ends on a summary of the sequence and 'notice what the next construction still leaves out'; ISO_Introduction opens 'A boundary made from values' and says outright 'The porous specimen in the previous room introduced the same distinction between values and visible form.' The entropy surface is a marching-cubes gyroid cut at a threshold (entropy_morphogenesis_vr.gd:197-209, LEVEL moves threshold_center), so ISO's LEVEL control continues exactly the question hall 9 opened.

reading.arc: The sequence takes one idea, a field of values cut at a chosen level, and walks it from a wireframe specimen to a building the visitor stands inside. The first seven halls each put a six-button desk beside an existing GPU field: the intro's LEVEL/SAMPLES, the fifteen-case MARGIN, the gallery's REPERTOIRE/LEVEL, the gyroid's PERIOD/INTRUSION/PROBE, the sculptor's PAIR/ADD/ERASE, the terrain's INTERIOR/TERMS/COLUMN, the portal's TERMS, and every desk has HOLD, which leaves a collisionless copy for comparison. The line of argument is that the same extractor serves different descriptions (chair, cup, gyroid, hand strokes, height fields, composed terms), and that boundary, enclosed volume and passage are three different questions. After ISO_Caves the halls lose their desks and shorten to 330-430 words: cave generation as authored distribution, animated noise as replacement rather than motion, metaballs as a sum crossing a threshold, raymarching as display without triangles, and the rhizome body as a graph with cycles turned into a shell you can enter. The close is right (a connection has to fit a body) but the last five chapters end in 'a useful extension would', describing instruments the rooms do not have.
holds: HOLD: eight of nine desks leave a held copy behind or beside the live specimen, always 'display copy, no collision'. The held-versus-live comparison is the sequence's carried method and its recurring object.

The refrain that a visible opening is not clearance for a body: intro (hole vs clearance), gyroid (the capsule probe and 'an untested wall must not become evidence of freedom'), terrain (the column counter 'does not decide'), portal, caves ('a counter is not a body'), rhizome ('a connection has to fit a body').

A name is an intention, the field makes the surface: Cup and Chair in the gallery, 'formula' on the gyroid desk, 'arched' on the terrain and portal desks, 'portal' in the caves, 'entropy' in the hall before.

The sampling budget as a standing number: 24/16/32 in the intro, then 64 per axis in the gallery, gyroid, sculptor and portal readouts, so 'a narrow feature can be absent from the mesh while present in its formula' recurs with a figure attached.
The desk grammar itself: 'Press X', a readout line, a RULE card, RESET that keeps the held copy. By the fourth hall the reader knows the instrument before reading the room.

Level as the movable line: 0.50/0.45/0.55 in the intro, 0.50 fixed while MARGIN moves the crossing, 0/-2/+4/+10 in the gallery, level one on the gyroid, level zero for the sculptor, the shell's wall in the rhizome.

hall_notes.note: The noise field as a blue specimen with pink triangle edges; LEVEL 0.50/0.45/0.55, SAMPLES 24/16/32 (13,824/4,096/32,768), HOLD to the right, 0.18 scale making 5.76 m. Every number and both code lines check against VoxelNoiseMarchingCubes.gd and iso_workshop.gd. Reads calmly and sets the three-question refrain (boundary, volume, passage).

The fifteen-case rack; MARGIN moves the values 0.30/0.70 to 0.14/0.54, 0.44/0.84, 0.48/0.88 and the crossing 0.50, 0.10, 0.85, 0.95 with masks fixed; TRACE's gold markers; arrangement 1 = table mask 254. Exact throughout and the 'which view invites you to forget the construction' question is the hall's best line. Says nothing about the Threshold Opinion standing nine cells further on.

Chair and cup; HOLD copies the middle-column pair; LEVEL 0 to -2 to +4 to +10 over all six fields; the cup as min(max(-inside, outside), handle); REPERTOIRE household/laboratory/abstract/survey; the cup vanishing at -2 with its labelled place left empty. The best-argued gallery hall; the close about escaping a name is a keeper.

Longest chapter. Torus at 'formula' (weights zero), gyroid with PERIOD 0.5/1/2/4 and INTRUSION erosion, modulation, warp; the quoted shader line is verbatim; the PROBE capsule (0.20/0.35/0.60 m, 1.70 m tall, 12 m rail) is the sequence's first honest clearance test and the chapter is careful about what it does not prove. Dense but every device earns its place.

Two deposits 0.90/0.65/0.45 m apart, radius 0.30; ADD/ERASE at a gold target with a quarter-metre brush; the cut as max(field, -brush); order as part of the form; the 500-edit memory. Strong lesson, but it carries 'In VR,' and a sentence of repair history the reader cannot use.

Turquoise height field with INTERIOR 0/0.3/0.4/0.8 and the 25x25 COLUMN counter; amber composed field with TERMS. Keeps the two experiments apart ('not a matched pair differing by one switch'), the code matches MarchingCubesFlat.glsl and the overhang shader, and the closing note honestly points at the CPU terrain and rhizome at the back.

The composed field with TERMS hillside to compound and a held bay of matching scale; fine sentences on names arriving before features and on a copy entering 'with different permissions'. But its one work is the same scene the reader just drove as the amber specimen next door, and the chapter presents it as a new landscape.

PORTALS 1/3/7/16 and BURIAL, the enclosing cave's PLUMB and OCTAVES 1/2/3/6, HOLD behind the cave; the queer cave gets two sentences. The closing four lines are the sequence's thesis. The enclosure claim ('above, beside and behind the eye') rests on a 2 %-scale bay token and a desktop-rig review, not a headset walk.

No desk. Compares this cave with the enclosing one and is honest that noise scale 13.5 vs 3.8, level 0.85 vs 0.88 and extent 300 vs 280 all changed at once. Silent about the second specimen on its stage, which is a hand-written sine tunnel, and it ends in an extension addressed to 'visitors'.

Replacement versus travel; correctly calls the blocks boundary-containing cells rather than a mesh (the extractor really emits whole cubes) and names the trig field and the 0.2 s rebuild. No desk; the mc_base tunnel beside the block set is unmentioned; ends in an extension.

Shortest hall. EMPLACE column/ring/pair/shell/scatter and KERNEL inverse square/Wyvill/Gaussian/cone over ten sources, HOLD behind. Three one-line regions for the secondary works; the 'small rear specimen' is the largest body in the room and the code block is pseudo-code fenced as gdscript.

Explains the ray march well (bounded steps and a finite tolerance are both in the shader: 80 steps, 0.001) and keeps display and collision apart. But it opens as a first meeting with a body the reader passed at the back of ISO_Caves and twice in ISO_Metaballs, and never says this placement's joins are set to 'necked'.

The plan as a graph with cycles, the shell, cut entrances, mesh and collision chunks: all of it is in rhizome_inside.gd (Kruskal tree plus extra edges, connectivity assert, abs(field) - wall). Asks the reader for a loop and distinguishes a planned cycle from a demonstrated return. A fitting close; the one hall where a two-line code excerpt is missing and would land.

stumbles: ISO_PortalLandscape: the reader has just pressed TERMS on this exact scene as the amber specimen in ISO_FlatTerrain; 'The landscape begins with hills' reads as a new object and the same glsl block is quoted twice.

ISO_Caves: 'The portal landscape is a promise made by a boundary' arrives one hall after Portal Landscape, whose chapter insisted its specimen was not a portal and had no rings; the reader must work out that a second, ringed portal landscape is meant.
ISO_Metaballs: 'The small rear specimen' is the same raymarched scene as 'the raymarched specimen nearby', standing at scale 1 (a 12 m box) against the nearby one's 0.2.

ISO_ImplicitModeling: 'Must a surface exist as a triangle mesh before you can see it?' was answered in one sentence in the previous hall, about the same body, which the reader has now met three times.

ISO_CaveGeneration: 'Compare this cave specimen with the one you have just inspected' and 'Both specimens' are ambiguous on a stage that holds two specimens, one of which is a striped stand-in tunnel and not a field.
ISO_Sculpting: 'In VR, move a controller' implies the reader might not be in the headset; the next paragraph's 'earlier implementation accidentally' sentence is a changelog.
ISO_Caves: 'A column can show several crossings, but a counter is not a body' sends the reader looking for a COLUMN readout that is two halls back.

ISO_LookupTable: the closing handover repeats 'description' three times, and the Threshold Opinion (five surfaces from one field, a resolution row, a brass rack of the fifteen) stands in the hall with no text.

ISO_CaveGeneration, ISO_AnimatedNoise, ISO_ImplicitModeling, ISO_RhizomeBody: four consecutive halls end in 'A useful extension would', addressed once to 'visitors', describing instruments the reader cannot press.

keep.quote: What matters is remembering that a smooth-looking silhouette at a distance does not erase the finite pieces from which this display is made.

Absence from the mesh does not establish absence from the underlying field, particularly where a feature falls between widely separated samples. Nor does a visible hole establish clearance for your body.
Which view lets you explain what just happened, and which invites you to forget the construction?
The cup need not remain a cup. But escaping its name will take more than changing the label.
If the generator omitted collision because the mesh was too costly, the desk says the probe is unavailable; an untested wall must not become evidence of freedom.
This instrument's memory helps make the body, and also decides what it can cease to remember.
Some changes are small; a new word on the desk can arrive more dramatically than a new feature in the surface.

A portal can be a hole that does not connect; an enclosing cave can be a room with no adequate entrance. The field supplies possibilities. A route is authored through width, collision and a body that can arrive.

reading.handover_in: Clean. Topology_Entropy_Morphogenesis closes softbodies on a sampled surface with LEVEL, NOISE and RESOLUTION controls and the line 'a body has become a set of relations'. ISO_Introduction picks it up by name ('The porous specimen in the previous room introduced the same distinction between values and visible form') and its own LEVEL/SAMPLES desk reads as a continuation of those controls rather than a restart. Nothing in the intro contradicts the morphogenesis hall.
reading.handover_out: Clean and deliberate. ISO_RhizomeBody ends by naming union, intersection and difference and reminding the reader they have met their consequences in joined chambers, wall shells and cut entrances; Boolean_Verbs opens on a box and a sphere and explicitly contrasts CSG with what came before ('Earlier, distance fields let a parameter round the meeting between forms. Here there is no smoothing band') and repeats the sequence's refrain that these exhibits have no collision. The only wrinkle is on the receiving side: Boolean_Verbs has no H1 title where every isosurfaces chapter does.

reading.arc: Three halls, each a step in scale. Verbs puts the three CSG operations on one box-and-sphere pair in one line down a hall, and plants the sequence's real subject in its second section: a region has an inside in the calculation but 'has not acquired the power to stop your body'. Gallery shows six families at every value of one named setting (24 placements, the only spine hall that places variants at all) and argues that the shipped default is an authored choice with neighbours. Works makes the negative big enough to promise architecture and lets exactly one work, the level-floored burrow, keep the promise with a collider; the wall, the SDF cavern, the rack and the workbench each offer an image of an interior or an action that the implementation withholds. The closing sections read the whole hall as a lesson in overpromising signs, then hand the question of accommodation to Swarm Intelligence. Every code excerpt and number in the three chapters checks against source; the weaknesses are in what the museum actually builds (pier colonnade, overlapping shells, works facing away, a wrong-handed instruction) and in a Works chapter that at 1710 words carries process notes a headset visitor cannot use. No bake or build record exists for any of the three halls in ada_run, so nobody has yet walked them in the museum.
holds: The box and the sphere: the same operand pair from the first bay through the workbench, the subtraction suite, the argument bench and the difference row.

The refrain 'inside in the calculation, no power to stop your body' (Verbs) answered by `stock.use_collision = walkable and spoil == "rock"` (Works, burrow) and closed by 'The shape of the cut and the rule for contact have to work together'.
The amber-and-blue coincident-face diagram, met in the Gallery and returning 'at the back wall' of Works to say what a picture can and cannot settle.

Defaults as authored choices: the Gallery's 'default becomes powerful when it is the only version we ever meet', which then bites (or fails to) when Works meets the workbench, the wall and the rack at their defaults.

One or two lines of source per work as captions, all verified: OPERATION_UNION (csg_union_demo.gd:313), the `in_b` lattice test (csg_intersection_demo.gd:341), OPERATION_SUBTRACTION + material_override (csg_difference_demo.gd:236-245), `if zeros >= 2: continue` (recursive_boolean_cube.gd:118), the cylinder carver (boolean_burrow.gd:272-275), `d = maxf(d, -_sd_sphere(p, c, r))` (sdf_cavern_room.gd:77), `col = color_a if (i % 2 == 0) else color_b` (coincident_face.gd:257).
A forward reference closing each chapter, each of which the next hall keeps (separated union in the Gallery; the negative getting large in Works; local rules in Swarm).

hall_notes.note: Walks the three verbs on one line (map cells (6,4), (6,12), (6,19)) and closes at the argument bench (4,22); prose is precise and every claim checks (48-cubed lattice, three decimals, forfeit:numeral plate under a body lifted 0.5, sills at rows 9 and 16 that the museum builds as 1 m raised floors under wall_height 3). Two things the visitor meets that the text does not: the template colonnade the plan stamps into this bare hall (piers on the centre line at rows 7, 15, 23 and two inside the bench chamber), and the six further stations of the bench itself (tree, seam, debt, architecture).

The strongest chapter as argument: each row is read as a walkable register and the default-first order is named as a catalogue convention. All 24 tokens resolve and the row order matches the walk (difference, union, intersection, breach, coincident, removal). As an encounter it is the weakest: row 23's four 5.35 m removal rooms stand at a 2 m pitch and row 15's middle benches sit in the aisle, every fronted work faces the far wall, and the colonnade stamps piers into two shells. CLAUDE.md's line that only Artist_Readymades places non-default values is stale; this hall places 24.

Nine works in the tall hall (wall_height 5, piers off, artifact_placement map). The burrow section is the sequence's payoff and reads exactly to the code (eleven carvers, cylinders, -0.02 to 2.28 m, collision only on rock). The chapter is four times the length of its neighbours; two passages read as backlog ('a specific possibility to develop', 'a precise unfinished task'), one sentence leaks the DNA-sweep measurement ('the museum's earlier image comparisons'), and the one bodily instruction sends the visitor to the wrong end of an 11 m block.

keep.quote: The region still has an inside and an outside in the calculation; it has not acquired the power to stop your body. Keep that difference with you when the objects become architecture.
Being connected and being smooth are different accomplishments.
Absence has been given a surface.
A default becomes powerful when it is the only version we ever meet. This row gives it neighbours.
A picture of a failure and an instance of that failure do different work. We can want the clarity of one without mistaking it for the other.

The shape of the cut and the rule for contact have to work together. A collider can enforce an opening too small to enter. A generous hollow without collision can make the wall beside it equally passable.
An equation over its head has supplied a room sooner than the construction has supplied an inside.
The large hollow may make us want another passage; wanting it does not yet give it a floor.

reading.handover_in: Clean. ISO_RhizomeBody closes with 'The next room names operations such as union, intersection and difference' and Verbs delivers exactly that on its first line; Verbs' union section reaches back ('Earlier, distance fields let a parameter round the meeting between forms. Here there is no smoothing band.'), and the rhizome's 'a connection has to fit a body' is the seed the burrow harvests two halls later. The only seam is formal: both neighbours open with an H1 and a question, the boolean chapters open on body text.
reading.handover_out: Loose. Works names Swarm Intelligence, states its premise correctly (many bodies, local rules) and ends on 'what space becomes possible among them?'; Physarum answers a different question (can a path remember where to grow) and cites the emergence rooms of sequence 12 as its precedent. Nothing contradicts, but the carried question is set down unanswered; one sentence in Works' last paragraph aimed at the trail field would close it.
