reading.arc: The sequence asks one question seven ways: when many bodies move together, what supplied the coordination? Physarum puts the memory in the ground; Flow Fields hands the ground a set of directions from outside; Boids removes the ground and makes neighbours the moving reference; the ABM hall gives agents state and a field that forgets at a rate the visitor sets; the ant colony splits the trail into a home channel and a food channel; the particle swarm moves memory inside the agent as a scored position; and the ecosystem adds a caretaker at population scale whose interventions are printed beside the box. Every chapter follows the same shape - watch one thing, the mechanism in plain words, what the picture cannot prove, a deferred experiment, a one-line handover - and every caveat re-says the sequence truth, that collective movement does not identify its cause. The arc lands cleanly on machine learning: inherited traits, environmental reward, and the rules that keep the experiment running.
holds: The refrain 'who or what supplied this': a field written versus a field given (Physarum/FlowFields), remembered visits versus remembered evaluations (ants/PSO), local events versus a caretaker (ecosystem) - each chapter re-asks the sequence truth in its own terms.

A one-line handover closing every chapter that names the next room's change of source: supplied direction -> neighbours -> internal state and a remembering environment -> two channels -> scored memory -> quieter rules that keep a system alive.

The 'watch the fading route, not the strong one' device: Physarum's abandoned path, FlowFields' surprising arrow, ABM's persistence versus width, ACO's less-reinforced food direction, PSO's place that was bright and is no longer.

Explicit back-references that chain the halls: FlowFields names Physarum; ACO names 'the previous room'; PSO names 'the ant colony's traces'; the capstone recaps 'A flock followed neighbours; ants read traces; particles pursued remembered scores.'

Repeatable beginnings as a method: RESET restores the same food, qualities and headings in the ant hall, and the same scatter and velocities in the swarm hall, so 'change one thing' can mean something.
One identical skeleton per chapter: H1, a one-line question, a single anchored work, eight to ten short paragraphs of roughly 400-570 words, a deferred experiment, the handover.

hall_notes.note: Opens on environmental memory: follow one bright connection through the twenty-second carousel of anchor layouts, then a junction, then the route that is fading. Reads as a patient watching instruction with the mechanism (sense ahead and to the sides, deposit, spread, decay, anchors emitting) given once in plain words; the organism the colony is named after is never named in the text.

The supplied field: predict an agent's turn from its arrow through the ten-second tour that ends parked in noise, with two small checks (same patch, different histories; near arrows, opposite directions). The cost-map paragraph and 'a field can give a direction without giving a destination' are the sequence's clearest mechanism prose; the closing 'future version' defers an axis the code already has.

One slider at a time on the highlighted boid's three arrows, then RADIUS with the weights held; the turn to 'who can each agent perceive' and 'alignment is not consent' carry the critical weight. It addresses one of the hall's five flocks and never mentions the other four.

The most experimental chapter: RESET as a repeatable beginning, EVAPORATE as how fast the ground forgets, ANTS as replacing the population while leaving its field, then RESET again to erase the marks. Reads well as a protocol; the map's catalyst foe, vent and prompter box are absent from the text, and the three MODE behaviours are counted but not named.

Two channels: outward ants seek food and leave home, returning ants the reverse; a destination is a state change rather than a bright place. Names stigmergy, refuses the optimisation claim the map title invites, and is the cleanest self-contained chapter of the seven.

The longest chapter: CONVERGE, SPREAD and NOVELTY as three scores put to the same bodies, the archive of two hundred, re-scoring memories, inertia. The strongest argument in the sequence ('Best is a relation between a position and an objective'), but the console's fourth button is missing from the text and the length shows in the second half.

The capstone: alternate scale between one encounter and the count, then read the POPULATION SUPPORT record beside the box and look back at the organisms. Recaps the sequence in one line, lands the truth - name the support before calling a thing self-organising - and hands over to machine learning without strain.

keep.quote: There is no little map hidden inside the moving dots. Information persists outside them, in a medium that changes what later movements are likely to do.
A field can give a direction without giving a destination.
Shared navigation can reproduce those decisions very efficiently. Efficiency alone cannot tell us whether every traveller can use the permitted route.
Alignment is not consent, and cohesion is not a complete account of belonging. These agents have no way to refuse a relation, remember harm or ask another agent for space.
Replacing the travellers and erasing their history are two different acts.
A destination is more than a bright place to reach: arriving there changes what information that ant will seek and leave on the next stretch.
Yesterday's high score cannot simply win against today's distances: the question has changed under it. The particle retains a place, but its claim to be best has to be renewed.
That comparison need not make intervention shameful. Care, repair and replenishment can be necessary. The question is whether they remain visible when someone describes the result as autonomous.

reading.handover_out: The capstone ends: 'Machine learning begins by asking what changes across generations. ML_Evolution answers it directly in its mechanism paragraph - 'The ecosystem in the previous room combined local behaviour with balancing interventions. reading.arc: The sequence walks from selection without a judge to a flag without an explanation, and in every hall performs the same separation: the operation a room really computes from the interpretation a label, a sign or a name lays over it. The first four halls (energy economy, three loss rules, k-means, backprop) are live computations the visitor can perturb and repeat; the sixth (sequence memory) is the one hall where the visitor's own hands set the parameters of an arithmetic they can predict before the slab moves. Halls five, seven and eight confess that a stage of the room is supplied rather than computed (typed-in names and percentages, scripted losses, a single fixed detection rule) and turn the confession into the lesson rather than hiding it. The last hall names the refrain outright (a cluster from a class, an edge from an object, a curve from generalisation) and closes on the anomaly as a relation between a point and the rule that judged it. The sequence's truth line, that a change in appearance is not yet evidence of learning, is honoured in every chapter; the cost is that three of the eight chapters are partly about what their room does not do.
holds: The refrain 'the operation is not the interpretation', built hall by hall (environment selects without a leaderboard; hill is a scoring rule not an obstacle; cluster is not a class; weight is not the answer; edge is not an object; gate is set by hand; scripted curve is not training; flag is not an error) and named explicitly in ML_Synthesis.

The 'hold something still' device: RESET and repeatable starts in the loss room, the same sample returning in k-means, four fixed examples in the network, three hand-set spheres in memory, one unchanging image in perception.

The honest confession as a structural beat: each chapter says in its own words what the room cannot yet show (a proposed comparison not offered; names supplied in advance; no models trained; a threshold not yet exposed) and turns it into the experiment the reader should want.

A backward callback in the fifth or sixth paragraph of every chapter (the ecosystem's caretaker; k-means moved centres; the fixed loss surface; the whole sequence's separations) and a one-sentence forward handover after the closing tag.

The ethical turn at the end of each hall: the outlier as a person the majority fit neglects, the cluster mistaken for an identity, the reference set's reward leaving unusual forms outside, the flagged point you would investigate rather than discard.
One tagged work per hall, opened with a second-person imperative (Find, Choose, Press, Carry) before any explanation.

hall_notes.note: Opens the sequence by asking whether the absence of a ranking means nothing selects, then explains the energy economy exactly as the code runs it (new cells pay, time drains, reproduction halves energy and nudges size, speed and colour) and insists the environment still prefers. Patient and clean; its one weakness is asking the eye to catch a birth among thirty bodies a centimetre or two across when the nameplate counts births and deaths.

Three error rules over one dataset, with OUTLIERS and RESET as the instruments for holding something still; every technical claim (squared vs Huber, the sine-plus-quadratic third surface, finite-difference gradient, bounded slope and intercept, outliers accumulating and returning with the slider) checks against the code, and the closing turn about the outlier as a person lands. RESET names a button the hall never labels.

The most hands-on hall: STEP, PAUSE / RUN, RESET and DATASET all exist, the sample really returns on RESET, and the BLOBS to RINGS to BLOCK cycle is precisely what the lesson controls do. The length is spent on watching rather than explaining, which is right. One slip: it calls the sequence a classification sequence.

Separates passing activity from a lasting weight, one wire from the aggregate error, fitting from generalising; correct about the four-example, four-input, two-output set and about what the backward pass does not do. Its instructions assume a training loop that is still running, which in the built hall stops fifty seconds after spawn with no way to restart it from a headset.

The clearest instance of the refrain: the Sobel step is real and the names and percentages are typed in, and the chapter says so. Accurate about the border zero and the local neighbourhood; it overstates what the moving window shows and never mentions that the room's own signs invite the visitor to paint pixels and grab filters, neither of which works.

The centrepiece, the longest chapter and the only one where the visitor's hands set the parameters; the arithmetic is right and the prose is the most alive in the sequence. But its flagship comparison puts the slab below the floor, its second run starts on an uncleared cell so the printed number will not match, and its height-to-value sentence and 'six decimals' do not match the code or the readout.

An honest chapter about a diagram: nothing trains, the losses are scripted, and the chapter specifies the experiment the room still needs. Its confession arrives in paragraph five, after four paragraphs that read as if a training process were in front of the visitor, who has meanwhile been standing at a panel that says so in two lines.

Names the refrain explicitly and closes the sequence on the anomaly as a relation; the Z-score arithmetic and the observation that the outer points sit inside the statistics that judge them are exactly what the code does. The painted threshold disc contradicts the boundary shape the chapter derives, and the mode sign the reader is sent to renders raw BBCode.

reading.handover_in: Clean. The swarm sequence closes on 'Machine learning begins by asking what changes across generations. Carry this distinction with you: inherited traits, environmental rewards and the rules that keep an experiment running all shape what can survive.' ML_Evolution opens on exactly that question (does anything select when no judge ranks?), and its sixth paragraph names the previous room explicitly ('The ecosystem in the previous room combined local behaviour with balancing interventions') before turning the caretaker motif into 'the apparently ordinary rule that pays for survival'. reading.handover_out: Sound. chapters_read: ML_Synthesis (last of machinelearning, for the handover in)
Euclid_Parallel (first of foundationscrisis, for the handover out)

reading.arc: Eight halls ask one question each of the same kind of object, a set of vertices and permitted connections, and each hall changes the question rather than the object. It opens by separating the graph from the order in which it is visited (two travellers on one tree), then from the positions used to draw it (a spring layout), then shows a route re-found when a connection is withdrawn (a stone sinks). The middle halls turn to what can be measured and claimed: drawn prominence against counted degree, directed reachability and the return path, the cheapest connecting skeleton against each traveller's own trip. The last two halls carry the sequence's real argument: a locally valid step (a forward push, a greedy pair) can close off a better arrangement, and only a procedure that can undo its own choices recovers it. The whole runs on the sequence truth (the same connections host different journeys; what the representation leaves out cannot be recovered by rerouting) and hands Foundations Crisis the distinction that a rule met is not a conclusion proved.
holds: The 'keep it in view' refrain: every hall opens with a short instruction to choose one element (a lamp, a vertex, a stone, an outer point) and hold it while the procedure runs, and the chapter then reads the procedure from that element's side rather than from the animation's confidence.

The carried object is the traveller's memory. The queue and stack of Foundations are picked up by name in Connectivity ('The stack you met with the two travellers now carries information about a question that remains open during the walk'), and the waiting branch of Foundations returns as the unmatched vertex of Matching.

Revision as the through-line of the second half: Pathfinding's replanning, Flow's missing reverse residual ('could some of what was sent earlier be taken back?'), Matching's 'Improving the first result requires undoing an accepted edge'. The exit lines chain it: 'Once again, an early acceptable choice may need to be undone.'

Representation before value: each hall ends by refusing to let its measure stand for worth. Waiting time behind a neat animation, 'an unsupported story about influence', ''Minimum' refers to that sum, not to every traveller's individual journey', 'Maximising a count cannot establish consent, suitability or fairness'.

One shape for eight chapters: a title, a one-line question, one anchored work, six or seven paragraphs at about 400 words, an exit line naming the next hall's question. The sameness is what makes the sequence feel like one voice; at length it is also a stumble (see the backlog paragraphs).

hall_notes.note: Breadth-first and depth-first on a fifteen-lamp tree that alternates by itself; the chapter moves from watching to naming (queue, stack) and closes on waiting time as the ordering rule's consequence. Reads cleanly, but the hall's own readout names the two travellers THE TIDE and THE DIVER and the chapter never does.

The connection-versus-coordinate distinction on an eight-vertex cube drawn by springs and repulsion; the exercise of naming an endpoint by its neighbours instead of by left/right is the sequence's best small task. 'Its positions are adjustable' invites a grab nothing answers, and the drawing settles once with no way to re-tangle it.

A spark commutes across stepping stones on the engine's AStar3D; a push button sinks a stone on its route, three at most, the oldest resurfacing. The chapter's care about 'the graph the search can use' is exact; it trips by asking the reader to watch a displayed, highlighted, bright route that is only ever the spark's walk.

The one chapter that says openly the room cannot yet do what its title asks, and turns that into a method: count degree yourself against a display whose centralities are assigned. Honest and useful, but its first instruction sends the visitor to 'displayed network measures' that are two inert ball-on-bar meters with no number on them.

Strongly connected components by Tarjan's single pass; the advice to test a proposed component from more than one start and the 'one additional return connection' observation are strong teaching. It relies on watching the moment components are discharged together, and the run happens once, seconds after the hall builds, with no in-world restart.

Kruskal on a ten-vertex euclidean graph, accept/reject read as a cycle check; the shift from 'cheap connection' to 'surviving a failure' is the sequence's clearest turn of question. The watch-the-next-edge exercise is undercut by the code: considered edges turn yellow and stay yellow whether they were accepted or rejected.

Forward-only push/relabel with capacity, flow, excess and height as four named quantities, and the BLOCKED end state made into the lesson rather than hidden. The most carefully revised chapter; the negative excess printed on the source sphere is the one readout its definitions do not cover.

The payoff: a five-cycle with five spokes, ORDER/STEP/RUN/RESET push buttons, three pairs versus five from the same connections, and every number checks against the scan order in the code. The longest and the best chapter; one sentence about the source file name is a developer's aside inside a visitor's room.

stumbles: GT_Pathfinding: 'Watch the displayed route change', 'the newly highlighted one', 'a bright route is the spark's calculated route'. No route is drawn; there is the spark's hop-by-hop walk and a readout saying 'route: N stones'. The reader looks for a line and finds none.

GT_Network_Analysis: 'Then look at the displayed network measures. Ask which of those quantities you could independently check'. The scene's two meters never move and carry no number, and 'an animated number appears authoritative' describes nothing in the hall.
GT_Layout: 'Its positions are adjustable'. A headset visitor reaches for a vertex; the artifact takes no input at all.

GT_Layout: 'Keep those relationships in view while the drawing settles'. The layout settles once from the frame the hall builds, and a visitor walking the seven cells from the spawn may meet a drawing that has finished moving, with nothing to restart it.

GT_Connectivity, GT_Spanning_Trees, GT_Flow: 'Watch the moment several vertices receive one component colour', 'Watch the next edge considered by the display', 'Watch for a PUSH or RELABEL step' each describe a one-shot run whose only restart is a keyboard action. Matching's button panel is the model the other three lack.

GT_Spanning_Trees: a rejected edge is never marked and the current-edge yellow is never cleared, so after the first rejection 'the next edge considered' is one yellow line among several, and the green tree is drawn as a second line over yellow at the same coordinates.
GT_Foundations: 'One traveller... The other...' while the readout beside the lamps alternates THE TIDE - BFS and THE DIVER - DFS; the reader has to make the match unaided.
GT_Flow: the green source sphere reads a negative e: value while the chapter defines excess as 'more has arrived than has yet left'.
GT_Matching: 'The artifact retains the source name `edmonds_algorithm`'. The visitor sees GREEDY MATCHING on the caption and never a file name; a backticked token in reader prose.

Sequence-wide: six of eight chapters end on a 'future/proposed extension' paragraph, so the last movement before each exit is a promise about a room that does not exist, and the exits lose their push.

keep.quote: The waiting branch has not disappeared from the graph. It has changed position in the procedure’s pending work.
A queue spreads attention across a frontier; a stack carries it into a branch.
If a claim about the network disappears when the drawing rotates or rearranges, ask whether the claim belonged to the graph or to its presentation.
Search cannot use an option the representation never supplies.
A long and fragile return journey counts as a return journey under this definition.
Redundancy changes meaning when the question changes from cheap connection to surviving a failure.
It leaves us with a question: could some of what was sent earlier be taken back?
Nobody has gained a new connection. We changed which possibility was considered first.

reading.handover_in: ML_Synthesis exits: 'Graph theory will give us another representation of relations. Instead of asking how far points lie from a centre, we will ask which points are connected and what those connections permit.' GT_Foundations opens: 'Can two travellers obey the same connections and encounter the graph in different orders?' The words 'connections' and 'permit' carry straight across (the sequence is titled 'What Connections Permit'), and the machine-learning habit of separating the operation from its interpretation ('A detector's name cannot supply evidence that its flags are useful') is exactly the habit graph theory applies to 'important', 'minimum' and 'maximum'. Registers match: both chapters are about 400 words on the same template. Clean.
reading.handover_out: GT_Matching exits: 'The foundations sequence will question what a formal system can establish. Carry one distinction forward: a procedure meeting its local rule is not automatically a proof of its strongest advertised conclusion.' Euclid_Parallel opens on a plaque counter wrapping (`(current_postulate + 1) % 5`) and reaches 'A rule can feel inevitable long before we have established that it follows', so the thread (rule met is not conclusion proved) lands. The register breaks hard, though: Euclid_Parallel is 1,709 words against Matching's 574, seven numbered sections with headings, five gdscript excerpts, draw tags, a two-voice dialogue ('Fair — and let's say what the array does about it') and a source-editing aside ('In the source, move Line3's offset out to 0.4'). The visitor steps from eight uniform rooms into an annotated source reading. The GT exit line does its job; one concrete foothold (the plaque, the gold) would ease the jump, and the rest is the next sequence's to absorb.

reading.arc: Foundations Crisis walks one habit through seven materials and then turns it on the project itself: find the instrument, read what it actually measures, and name the gap between that and its caption. Euclid's hall plants the method in a plaque whose gold arrives before the argument and a triangle that prints sixties it never measured; NonEuclid changes the host and makes 180 degrees one answer among three; Russell withdraws the permission to collect everything; Godel separates a stopped search from a proof that no search can succeed. Escher moves the question into where you stand, Brouwer into what you have made versus what you assert about every continuation, Florensky into what follows when reports conflict and who still gets through. Crisis_Synthesis brings in the QFEP formula as a sentence with handles and applies the sequence's habit to it (colour on a rail is a proposal, a total can hide its compensations) before handing the lit formula to the laboratory. The stance is consistent and rare: every apparatus is described as smaller than its claim, and the prose treats that as the lesson rather than an apology.
holds: The refrain 'what did this number depend on?': each hall ends on an instrument that measures less than its caption (three sixties, a stopped prover arm, a move counter, a flickering lamp, complementary opacities, a finite orbit sample), and the prose names the shortfall every time instead of hiding it.

Carried works, all confirmed in the map layers: the triangle (Euclid -> NonEuclid -> Brouwer), the parallel lines (Euclid -> Brouwer), the postulates plaque (Euclid -> Russell), and in Synthesis the Russell workbench, the set box, the staircase, the sphere and the Godel plaque return.

The distinction handed in from GT_Matching (a procedure meeting its local rule is not a proof of its strongest advertised conclusion) recurs as the prover that jams, the prefix that proves nothing about every continuation, the diagonal that displays no completed infinity, the counter that 'does not prove chaos'.
The small verbatim excerpt as the whole of an apparatus: `% 5`, two Booleans, `terms.append(value)`, `_d[i] = 1 - _list[i][i]`, `x = r * x * (1.0 - x)`, each used the same way: this is all it does.
Closings on the body and the floor: 'The floor has not moved. Your account of it has.'; 'You are allowed to leave it.'; 'It has made a small part wait for it.'
Each last paragraph names the next hall's question, so the reader crosses every threshold knowing what to ask.

hall_notes.note: Seven numbered sections read the build: the plaque's `% 5` loop and its gold branch, three unevenly spaced lines, a triangle labelled 60/60/60 that measures 53.1/63.4/63.4, a screen drawing a grid before anything arrives. Reads as a code-reading essay addressed to a walker, the longest chapter in the arc, and the one whose register slips most between 'Walk between the columns' and 'In the source, move Line3'.

The bench's HOST slider (PLANE / SPHERE / DISK) rebuilds a triangle per host and asks its corners; Gauss-Bonnet is named and held at arm's length ('one changing display is not a proof'). Reads cleanly and ends on the sequence's best closing line; the side works are described faithfully except the curvature slider, which ships as a number readout, not a surface sketch.

IN / OUT at cell 5, then 'within U' at cell 6; the box, braces, barber, liar and hotel are sorted into contradiction versus offended expectation. The argument is precise and the two-Boolean excerpt is the code; the floor texts (IF IT DOES / IT DOESN'T) go unmentioned but do no harm.

A stopped prover arm and a sorter with a gold gap; the prose is careful (three kinds of failed search, soundness named) but anchors two of ten placed works, wears a different template (H1, question line, no sections, inline link) and is a third the length of its neighbours. The floor slogans say what the chapter asks the reader not to say yet.

STEP around a tabletop model whose console adds up ascent and descent; FORM cycles five constructions (RETURN SIDE, CLOSING DROP, OPEN RUN, SCAFFOLD, TILTED TREADS); then the green bead at the Penrose beams and the trident's two-into-three. Every control, name and number checks against escher_staircase_study.gd; the most physically grounded hall in the arc.

'Wait before touching anything': two buttons append to a prefix the program has not stored ahead; excluded middle as a reading slider; the sqrt2^sqrt2 case split; Cantor's finite diagonal; a timed staircase for contrast. Faithful to code (256 / 10 / 32 bits, blue and amber beads); the one slip is 'nearby' for a work at the other end of the hall.

Walk through a closed leaf; three buttons hold P and not-P without the alarm following; the sphere keeps A and not-A; the two quantum toys at the back are refused as certificates. Strong on non-explosion versus dialetheism; the Schrodinger paragraph is written from a desk.

The formula with three reading buttons and two disputed rails; the logistic map under its own r; the atrium's 1:10 model; five returning works; a closing turn to whose possibilities an arrangement sustains. As source it is the arc's best synthesis; as rendered, an unclosed code fence swallows its second half and all three footnotes.

stumbles: Crisis_Synthesis: the code fence at line 43 is two backticks, so everything after `x = r * x * (1.0 - x)` (atrium, returning works, closing section, three footnotes) renders as one monospace block.

Godel_Incompleteness: 443 words for a hall of ten works; eight pass without a sentence, and the floor under the visitor says 'SELF-REFERENCE IS THE EDGE' three rooms after Russell called that lesson too thin.

Euclid_Parallel section 6: 'So we open on the fallback: `_point_mode = true`' describes a scan this map never runs; the token `#mode:grid` sets GRID VIEW explicitly and the screen draws sixteen by sixteen empty cells.
Florensky_Paraconsistent: 'on a desktop click, a randomly chosen ALIVE or DEAD result' is a desktop aside; in the headset the box's input handler returns and the lid never opens.
Crisis_Synthesis: the first sentence, 'A formula waits in the next room', is read while standing four cells from the formula.

NonEuclidean_Spaces: 'changes its own surface sketch' for a slider placed without a witness token, which builds no surface; and the heading 'The surfaces beside the bench' for works at the far end of the hall.
Brouwer_Intuitionism: 'The nearby sum over hypotheses' after the triangle and lines at the back, for a work standing beside the choice bench at the front.
Euclid_Parallel: 'In the source, move Line3's offset out to 0.4' asks a visitor to edit a scene file; 'three placements ship them' counts corridor and test copies; 'isoceles'.
Crisis_Synthesis: 'The plaque, the nested box and the staircase return as reminders', but the Godel plaque was never introduced, so for the reader it appears here for the first time.

keep.quote: Count once more: five postulates, three lines, one triangle, one screen, two rows of pillars. Every number is true. Not one of them is necessary.
For now, return the slider to PLANE. The floor has not moved. Your account of it has.
The arrows turn around the same disc. Your hand has somewhere to go; the proposed set does not.
That matters because a slow search, a broken search and a proof that no search can succeed are three different things.
The mark offers a place from which to believe the image. You are allowed to leave it. What else becomes convincing only when we remain in the assigned place?
This room has not made the world obey your hand. It has made a small part wait for it.
The visible assertion "closed" has no authority to stop you. Someone had to make that decision. A system can preserve conflicting descriptions and still have to decide who gets through.
The earlier rooms have not proved it. An equals sign can gather a desire before we know how to measure it.

reading.handover_in: GT_Matching ends by naming the foundations sequence and handing over one distinction: a procedure meeting its local rule is not automatically a proof of its strongest advertised conclusion. Euclid_Parallel never repeats the phrase, but its whole method is that distinction applied (the plaque's gold branch, the triangle's shipped sixties, the screen's grid before data) and its last lines answer it directly ('Every number is true. Not one of them is necessary'). The join is clean if implicit; the only friction is register: the reader leaves a 574-word hall with one control and enters a 1709-word hall with seven code excerpts and instructions that sometimes address an editor rather than a walker.
reading.handover_out: Crisis_Synthesis ends 'Leave the formula lit. We will meet it again in the laboratory, where particular implementations give its terms consequences', and QFEP_Introduction opens 'In the previous room, the formula waited to be questioned. Here it returns a number'. A clean pass; QFEP_Introduction even corrects an expectation Crisis sets ('Move phi through zero') by noting its own phi rail is nonnegative. Two wrinkles on the Crisis side: its opening line 'A formula waits in the next room' belongs to Florensky's exit, not this hall's entrance, and its unclosed code fence means the reader arrives at the laboratory having read the synthesis's second half as monospace.

reading.arc: The sequence takes the formula the crisis synthesis left lit and makes it return a number, then takes that number apart term by term. A console where four rails give one total (Introduction) is followed by a bit grid that separates a source's uncertainty from a predictor's misses (F), a fan that counts endings and closures (E), a hall where a lambda value becomes a lit route the visitor can move (Lambda), a signed rail whose old moral labels appear only on request (Phi), a reaction-diffusion pair that separates the model from the way it is stepped (Edge of Chaos), a receiver that can be connected and cut (Sandbox), and a jar body whose stiffness, damping and pressure the two weights drive (Synthesis). Every hall runs the same discipline: do the operation, name what changed, then say what was supplied rather than measured, who wrote the mapping, and what the count, colour or route cannot decide. The Q of QFEP is carried as a question of revisability, who may change the terms, rather than as a claim, and the sequence closes by turning that question on the maker (Self-Q) and handing 'whose distinctions are compressed' to the post-crisis sequence.
holds: The supplied-versus-measured refrain: every hall closes its operation with a limit stated in the same voice ('its fixed change value is not an observed rate', 'not quantities measured by this fan', 'a curatorial argument', 'visual feedback for its own value', 'Someone wrote this mapping', 'does not establish that nature uses the same numerical scale').

A chain of last-line handovers: each chapter's final sentence names the next hall's question (predictability, then counting alternatives, then invitation, then sign, then driving a pattern, then where control reaches, then what a body keeps, then compression).
Two carried controls, LAMBDA and PHI, reappear in five halls with their ranges explicitly compared, and the reader is trained on 'Read the rail as well as the letter' before trusting a symbol.

The 'you can do X; you cannot yet do Y' figure: reopen but not grow (E), move the light but not the rows (Lambda), hide the labels but carry them (Phi), connect and cut but not invent another response (Sandbox). Each apparatus's limit is stated as the next freedom.
Predict-before-reading instructions: guess before reading H, count leaves before the readout, describe persistence before naming a regime, name direction before magnitude.
Self-Q bookends: introduced in the first hall as the return of the question to the maker, closed in the last hall with 'Which part of the apparatus would we change next?'

hall_notes.note: The balance workbench: four 0-1 rails, KEEP outline, nearest-of-seven reference. Sets the sequence's method (two arrangements, one number; what the total lost) and introduces QFEP, Q and Self-Q with the two footnotes the whole sequence leans on. Densest chapter; the arithmetic paragraph arrives before the letters are named.

The Shannon workbench: p rail, bit grid, EXPECT 0/1 with amber misses. Cleanly separates source uncertainty from a predictor's fit and ends on the sharpest line of the sequence about who has to change. Reads fast and true; 'the room's F term' is its one loose phrase.

The entropy fan: CYCLE / ONE / OPEN / PRUNE, 81 leaves, 27 under 18 closures, nats versus bits. Counting is made physical, and the PRUNE / OPEN pair carries the ethical turn (reopening a route on a screen versus in a life) without preaching.

The lambda hall: an authored spectrum made walkable, then the LIT STRIP console (0.20-0.80, RETURN) lets the visitor move the recommendation and watch the rows refuse to follow. 'Light has made a recommendation, not cleared a passage' is the hall's whole argument. One slip: 'Changing the sign' in a hall with no sign.

The signed rail (particles up or down, EARLIER LABELS reveals RESIST / EMBRACE) and the transforming pattern that runs independently of PHI. Direction-then-magnitude is taught well; the lambda promenade on the way out is never mentioned, and the 'at zero' claim is only true at the start.

Two screens, same start and time, one at half the step (DT .3 / .15, HOLD / RUN, B difference). The chapter's distinction between model time, step size and SIM SPEED is exact and valuable. It trips on 'the earlier calculation' (a changelog the visitor never saw) and on a second, unwired LAMBDA rail by the door that it does not name.

Two handles, one receiver, CONNECT / CUT and REPEAT, a console that prints offered and used values. The cut-route memory ('It has not restored an innocent beginning') and 'Someone wrote this mapping' land. The neighbouring particle field is correctly described as not joined (its listener group is never populated).

The morphology specimen: its own LAMBDA and PHI, PAIR A/B/C, PULSE / STEADY, a plate of stiffness, damping, drag and pressure. Separates imposed breathing from the body's own motion and closes the sequence with Self-Q and a clean hand to post-crisis. The floor's EGG / IMAGO / RETURN TRANSFORMED inscriptions contradict its refusal to read the jar as an assay of life.

stumbles: QFEP_Edge_Of_Chaos: 'move LAMBDA slowly. Give the image time to respond' - the LAMBDA rail three cells from the spawn is a separate slider whose #locked:0.4 token does nothing (it moves freely and drives nothing in the hall); the console the chapter means is on the east side and is never located.
QFEP_Lambda_Spectrum: the chalkboard beside the entrance reads 'life at λ ≈ 0.4' while the chapter says the chosen value 'is not a universal threshold at which life, creativity or queerness appears'.
QFEP_Synthesis: the floor says EGG, THE PLINTH OF BECOMING, IMAGO, RETURN TRANSFORMED while the chapter says 'A responsive specimen is not an assay of queerness or a test for life'.
QFEP_Lambda_Spectrum: 'Changing the sign does not erase the arrangement' - there is no sign to change in this hall; sign is the next hall's word.

QFEP_Edge_Of_Chaos: 'The earlier calculation could produce a pattern largely through overshooting and clipping its values' - the visitor never saw an earlier calculation; the paragraph reads as a changelog.
QFEP_Phi_Term: a 4.34 m rail of eight bodies with lambda numerals stands between the transforming pattern and the exit, unmentioned in the hall that was introduced with 'Phi introduces time'.
QFEP_Phi_Term: 'At zero, no new particles are released' - true only for the configured start; a hand cannot return the continuous rail to exact zero, so after the first move the emitter never stops.
QFEP_F_Term: 'The room's F term asks a related but different question' - the room contains no F device; the visitor looks for one.
QFEP_Introduction: the previous chapter promised 'We will meet it again in the laboratory', and the lit formula does hang at the back of this hall, but the chapter never turns to it.

QFEP_Synthesis: 'Breathing varies around that pressure baseline within an interval the maker selected' - the reader is not told that breathing only runs while lambda sits between 0.3 and 0.7, so the plate's STEADY outside that band looks like a failed button.
QFEP_Edge_Of_Chaos: 'Keep a record in words' - a headset visitor has nothing to write on.

keep.quote: One number can summarise several contributions while concealing how they compensated for one another. Keeping the separate values visible prevents a convenient summary from becoming the whole account.
A familiar symbol does not guarantee the same range. Read the rail as well as the letter.
Here you can change the expectation with one button. Elsewhere a system might insist that the world change instead. Keep that difference with you.
Outside this little machine, reopening a route may not restore the lives or histories lost when it closed. The ease of the button is part of the experiment's limit.
Stay with the difference between more endings on a screen and more ways to live.
Light has made a recommendation, not cleared a passage.
Disconnection has left a memory of your action. It has not restored an innocent beginning.
Steady pressure is something you have given it. Stillness would be something else.

reading.handover_in: Clean in voice and in claim. Crisis_Synthesis ends 'Leave the formula lit. We will meet it again in the laboratory, where particular implementations give its terms consequences' and 'An equals sign waits'; QFEP_Introduction opens 'In the previous room, the formula waited to be questioned. Here it returns a number.' Both keep the formula a research proposal rather than a law, and the crisis chapter's caution about ΔE needing a duration is honoured by the console's 'fixed change value is not an observed rate'. The one loose thread is physical: the formula the visitor was told to leave lit hangs again at the back of the introduction hall (qfep_formula_3d at map_data.json:592, floor label THE FORMULA at :346) and the chapter never acknowledges the reunion it promised.
reading.handover_out: Clean. QFEP_Synthesis ends 'Post-crisis begins with representation itself. After learning to name a model's choices, ask whose distinctions those choices make clear and whose they compress', and CriticalAlgorithms_Algorithmic_Bias_Visualization opens on exactly that: 'Which differences become difficult to recognise when a representation gives some words less room?' with a COMPRESSION handle. The Self-Q closing paragraph and the next hall's 'Both groups were chosen' share one question. Nothing to fix here.

reading.arc: The sequence takes the museum's closing question, 'knowing the limits of formalisation, what do we build?', and answers it as a chain of design decisions the visitor can operate rather than admire: how much room a representation gives a distinction (bias), what a seating plan decides before anyone speaks (ethics), what a resolved disagreement deletes (paraconsistency), where a verdict is spoken from (situated), what a count of contributions hides and who may revise (collective), which connections a body can enter and which it can only see (rhizome), and how a body's pose and its neighbours can be changed by hand (laboratory). Each hall follows one rhythm: an instruction to press or move something, a short code excerpt introduced by 'The source makes the operation inspectable', a paragraph stating exactly what the exhibit does not establish, and a question to carry out. The visitor's own alteration in the laboratory is written to a pose record and stands again in the final hall beside the body it began from, where the ledger shows what the record kept and what it could not. The book closes by turning the question back on the maker (what would you want the record to keep next, which change do you still want to make) and by circling to the first hall's counter that was already running when we arrived.
holds: The refrain 'The source makes the operation inspectable' with a verified excerpt in six of the eight halls, always followed by a sentence about what the code does not prove (a picture of a decision, not a proof; equal spacing, not equal opportunity).

A 'what this exhibit cannot establish' paragraph in every hall: authored positions not measured embeddings; supplied percentages not calibrated probabilities; a simulation of accretion not a live editor; composed passages not a grown network; authored targets not discovered destinations.

The carried object: the hand you moved. The laboratory's released pose crosses to the final hall through AssemblyPoseRecord, and the last line ('The clock is still running') returns to Point_One's counter.
Keeping the subject constant while the frame changes: same words, less room; same subject, four verdicts; same points, other connections; same hand, another neighbour.

Every hall ends by naming the next version it would want (a named model and documented measurement, observed sightlines, a small rule table, a criterion per panel, a browsable history, a new opening in the wall, another joint, the path of the hand), so the sequence's 'return with a change' is rehearsed seven times before the final hall asks for it.

Buttons in small caps as the prose's verbs (READ, PAIR, RESOLVED, COVER, DISPUTE, VERSION, HANG AGAIN): the visitor's operations are the chapter's paragraphs, and every named control exists on the artifact's console.

hall_notes.note: Opens the sequence on the COMPRESSION handle: two coloured word groups, one lerp, and the difference between being present and being tellable-apart. The tightest chapter in the sequence; every claim matches bias_from_inside.gd, and READ hands the reader the maker's own caveat ('Both groups were chosen').

Five seating plans on one console (HEAD, CIRCLE, PAIR, WATCH, VACANT) plus the COLOUR/NEUTRAL persuasion switch. Its cadence is press-then-think, close to a guided operation, but each press earns its thought and the refusal to let geometry stand in for participation is exact.

Four authored pictures of a disagreement; the RESOLVED stump ('look down for B') is the hall's best moment. The formal paragraph on explosion is honest about the limit of the analogy, but the one citation is a bare hyperlink a headset reader cannot follow.

One subject, four verdicts, three ways of showing an address (FOOTNOTE, COVER, WITNESS). The 'dangerous to whom, under which circumstances' passage is the strongest accountability writing in the sequence. The spider is introduced in the last paragraph, after ten paragraphs that tell the reader to linger.

Two works: the helix workbench (FLOW, COLOUR, PIECE, DISPUTE, REVISE, VERSION) and the round table with no head. The counting passage is accurate to the readout but narrates a label change the reader never saw; the table's cards are described as turned toward different approaches, which the code does not build.

Cave first (the violet junction, the overcrossing you cannot turn at, the minf union that lets two volumes share an interior), grower second (one link or three, cut a busy point, the ring that does not spread). The best prose in the sequence, but the reading order is the reverse of the walk, and the opening question line is dropped.

The longest hall by 650 words: a hand you can leave too far away, an inventory finding authored targets, one rerouteable connection that makes and unmakes a loop, a ragdoll that falls, and a chair, table and lamp that pull apart. Every mechanical claim matches the scripts; the reader carries thirteen joint names with no heading to rest on.

Two bodies (blue start, amber kept) and a ledger that reads the same record; the argument that the destination survives while the gesture does not is exact and moving ('The hand has arrived. Your hand is missing.'). Closes the book by circling to the first hall's counter; one ledger sentence is garbled.

keep.quote: Presence in a representation is therefore different from being represented with useful distinctions.
Equal spacing is what this loop guarantees. Equal opportunity to speak would require another kind of evidence.
Its useful first gesture is spatial: an unresolved relation can be represented without erasing the parts that made the relation difficult.
A favourable word also needs criteria; situatedness is not a licence to stop checking an appealing claim.
The table has no head. The classification still has an author.
We have not escaped geometry by drawing a network. We have acquired another place to work on it.
A body can look as though it is coming into being while it is coming into agreement with a description.
The hand has arrived. Your hand is missing.
